modules.title: The Lorentz Group
modules.doc:
We define the Lorentz group.

## References

* Lorentz Transformations, Rotations, and Boosts, Jaffe.
  <https://cdn.ku.edu.tr/cdn/files/amostafazadeh/phys517_518/phys517_2016f/Handouts/A_Jaffi_Lorentz_Group.pdf>.

sections.text:
## Matrices which preserves the Minkowski metric

We start studying the properties of matrices which preserve `ηLin`.
These matrices form the Lorentz group, which we will define in the next section at `lorentzGroup`.
# The Lorentz group as a group
## Lorentz group as a closed subset of matrices

## Lorentz group as a topological group

We now show that the Lorentz group is a topological group.
We do this by showing that the natural map from the Lorentz group to `GL (Fin 4) ℝ` is an
embedding.

## Lorentz group as a closed subgroup of the general linear group

Following the plan sketched by PrParadoxy and Joseph Tooby-Smith in physlib issue #833, we realise
`LorentzGroup d` as a *closed* subgroup of `GL (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ`. This promotes the closed
embedding into the ambient matrix space (`isClosedEmbedding_val`) to the level of the general
linear group, and is the structural prerequisite for a Lie group structure on the Lorentz group.

The remaining step of that plan, endowing `LorentzGroup d` with a Lie group structure as a closed
subgroup of the Lie group `GL (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ` and thereby deriving its Lie algebra, needs the
closed subgroup theorem (Cartan's theorem: a closed subgroup of a Lie group is an embedded Lie
subgroup). That theorem is not yet available in Mathlib: there is no `LieSubgroup`, and no
`ChartedSpace`/`IsManifold` instance is produced from a closed embedding (only
`IsOpenEmbedding.singletonChartedSpace`, for open embeddings). The Lie group instance and the
Lorentz algebra therefore remain open; see the `TODO` at the top of this file.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.range_toGL
declarations.doc:
The range of `toGL`, as a set in `GL (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ`, is exactly the preimage of the
Lorentz group under the coercion `GL (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ → Matrix _ _ ℝ`: an element of the general
linear group lies in the image precisely when its underlying matrix is a Lorentz transformation.
declarations.statement:

    Set.range (@toGL d).toFun =
      Units.val ⁻¹' (LorentzGroup d : Set (Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ))

`GL (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ`. This strengthens `toGL_embedding`: the image is closed because it is the
preimage, under the continuous coercion `GL (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ → Matrix _ _ ℝ`, of the closed set
`LorentzGroup d` (`LorentzGroup.isClosed`).
declarations.statement: lemma toGL_isClosedEmbedding : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding (@toGL d).toFun

modules.doc:
## Boosts applied to Lorentz vectors

These recover what one would describe as the ordinary Lorentz transformations
of Lorentz vectors.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Vector.boost_time_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_time_eq (i : Fin d) (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) (p : Vector d) :
    (boost i β hβ • p) (Sum.inl 0) = γ β * (p (Sum.inl 0) - β * p (Sum.inr i))

declarations.name: Lorentz.Vector.boost_inr_self_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_self_eq (i : Fin d) (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) (p : Vector d) :
    (boost i β hβ • p) (Sum.inr i) = γ β * (p (Sum.inr i) - β * p (Sum.inl 0))

declarations.name: Lorentz.Vector.boost_inr_other_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_other_eq (i j : Fin d) (hji : j ≠ i) (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) (p : Vector d) :
    (boost i β hβ • p) (Sum.inr j) = p (Sum.inr j)

declarations.name: Lorentz.Vector.boost_toCoord_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_toCoord_eq (i : Fin d) (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) (p : Vector d) :
    (boost i β hβ • p) = fun j =>
      match j with
      | Sum.inl 0 => γ β * (p (Sum.inl 0) - β * p (Sum.inr i))
      | Sum.inr j =>
        if j = i then γ β * (p (Sum.inr i) - β * p (Sum.inl 0))
        else p (Sum.inr j)

modules.title: Coordinate-axis boosts in `SL(2,ℂ)` and the Lorentz group
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

We define the axis-indexed lift `Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis` in `SL(2,ℂ)` and its image
`LorentzGroup.boostAxis` in the Lorentz group.

The parameter `t ≠ 0` is multiplicative; replacing `t` by `t⁻¹` reverses the boost. For
`t > 0`, its rapidity is `2 * log t`; negative values retain the action of the central
element `-1 : SL(2,ℂ)`.

For the `z`-axis, `LorentzGroup.boostAxis 2 t ht` agrees with the velocity-parameterized boost
`LorentzGroup.boost 2 β` at `β = (t² - t⁻²) / (t² + t⁻²)`.

The lift is Hermitian along every axis, and the `x`- and `y`-axis lifts are conjugates of
the diagonal `z`-axis lift.

The index `Sum.inl 0` is the time coordinate, while `Sum.inr 0`, `Sum.inr 1`, and
`Sum.inr 2` are the `x`, `y`, and `z` coordinates. Accordingly, axis indices `0`, `1`, and
`2` select the `x`-, `y`-, and `z`-axis boosts. The covering map uses the action
`X ↦ M X Mᴴ` on self-adjoint matrices.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis` defines the axis-boost lifts.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_inv` and `Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_conjTranspose` give their
  inverses and Hermiticity.
- `LorentzGroup.boostAxis` defines the induced Lorentz transformations, with entries given by
  `LorentzGroup.boostAxis_apply`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.exists_conj_boostAxis` proves that every lift is conjugate to the `z`-boost.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The axis-boost lift
- B. Axis conjugation
- C. The induced Lorentz transformation

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis
declarations.doc:
The `SL(2,ℂ)` lift of the boost along spatial axis `i`, with `0 = x`, `1 = y`, and
`2 = z`. The parameter `t` is multiplicative, and for `t > 0` the rapidity is `2 * log t`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def boostAxis : Fin 3 → (t : ℝ) → t ≠ 0 → SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_zero_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the `SL(2,ℂ)` boost lift along the `x`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_zero_apply (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (j k : Fin 2) :
    (boostAxis 0 t ht).1 j k =
      (!![((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2, ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2;
        ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2, ((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_one_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the `SL(2,ℂ)` boost lift along the `y`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_one_apply (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (j k : Fin 2) :
    (boostAxis 1 t ht).1 j k =
      (!![((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2,
        -Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2;
        Complex.I * ((t : ℂ) - (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2,
        ((t : ℂ) + (t : ℂ)⁻¹) / 2]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_two_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the diagonal `SL(2,ℂ)` boost lift along the `z`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_two_apply (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (j k : Fin 2) :
    (boostAxis 2 t ht).1 j k = (!![(t : ℂ), 0; 0, (t : ℂ)⁻¹]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_inv
declarations.doc: Inverting an axis boost replaces its multiplicative parameter `t` by `t⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_inv (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    (boostAxis i t ht)⁻¹ = boostAxis i t⁻¹ (inv_ne_zero ht)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: The matrix underlying an axis-boost lift is Hermitian.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_conjTranspose (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    (boostAxis i t ht).1ᴴ = (boostAxis i t ht).1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.boostAxis_eq_conj
declarations.doc: Every axis boost is obtained by conjugating the `z`-axis boost by `rotationZToAxis`.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_eq_conj (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    boostAxis i t ht =
      rotationZToAxis i * boostAxis 2 t ht * (rotationZToAxis i)⁻¹

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.exists_conj_boostAxis
declarations.doc: Every coordinate-axis boost is conjugate to the `z`-axis boost.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_conj_boostAxis (i : Fin 3) :
    ∃ R : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0),
      boostAxis i t ht = R * boostAxis 2 t ht * R⁻¹

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boostAxis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz transformation induced by the multiplicatively parameterized `SL(2,ℂ)` boost
along spatial axis `i`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def boostAxis (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) : LorentzGroup 3

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boostAxis_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of an axis boost in the Lorentz group.
declarations.statement:
lemma boostAxis_apply (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (boostAxis i t ht).1 a b =
      if a = Sum.inl 0 ∧ b = Sum.inl 0 then (t ^ 2 + (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2
      else if a = Sum.inl 0 ∧ b = Sum.inr i then -((t ^ 2 - (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2)
      else if a = Sum.inr i ∧ b = Sum.inl 0 then -((t ^ 2 - (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2)
      else if a = Sum.inr i ∧ b = Sum.inr i then (t ^ 2 + (t⁻¹) ^ 2) / 2
      else if a = b then 1 else 0

modules.title: Boosts in the Lorentz group
modules.doc:
Lorentz factors, finite coordinate boosts and their matrix entries.

## i. Overview

The Lorentz factor `γ β` determines a boost at speed `β`, with `|β| < 1`.
Parametrizing the speed by rapidity gives `γ (Real.tanh r) = Real.cosh r`.
The Minkowski signature has one positive time coordinate and negative spatial coordinates.
The time-space entries of a boost are `-γ β * β`.

## ii. Key results

- `γ_tanh`: the Lorentz factor expressed in terms of rapidity.
- `boost`: a Lorentz boost along one spatial coordinate.
- `boost_transpose_eq_self` and `boost_inverse`: transpose and inverse identities.
- `boost_inl_0_inr_self`: the active time-space matrix entry of a boost.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz factor
- B. Lorentz boosts
- C. Boosts in the zero-direction

## iv. References

The rapidity identity uses the hyperbolic-function identities in
`Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Artanh`.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.γ
declarations.doc: The Lorentz factor (aka gamma factor or Lorentz term).
declarations.statement: def γ (β : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.γ_tanh
declarations.doc: The Lorentz factor expressed in terms of rapidity.
declarations.statement: lemma γ_tanh (r : ℝ) : γ (Real.tanh r) = Real.cosh r

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.γ_zero
declarations.statement: lemma γ_zero : γ 0 = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.γ_neg
declarations.statement: lemma γ_neg (β : ℝ) : γ (-β) = γ β

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.γ_det_not_zero
declarations.statement: lemma γ_det_not_zero (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) : (1 - β^2) ≠ 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz boost with in the space direction `i` with speed `β` with
`|β| < 1`.
declarations.statement: def boost (i : Fin d) (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) : LorentzGroup d

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_transpose_eq_self
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_transpose_eq_self (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    transpose (boost i β hβ) = boost i β hβ

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_transpose_matrix_eq_self
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_transpose_matrix_eq_self (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    Matrix.transpose (boost i β hβ).1 = (boost i β hβ).1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_eq_id
declarations.statement: lemma boost_zero_eq_id (i : Fin d) : boost i 0 (by simp) = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inverse
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inverse (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    (boost i β hβ)⁻¹ = boost i (-β) (by simpa using hβ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inl_0_inl_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inl_0_inl_0 (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) = γ β

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_self_inr_self
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_self_inr_self (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr i) (Sum.inr i) = γ β

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inl_0_inr_self
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inl_0_inr_self (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr i) = - γ β * β

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_self_inl_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_self_inl_0 (i : Fin d) {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr i) (Sum.inl 0) = - γ β * β

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inl_0_inr_other
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inl_0_inr_other {i j : Fin d} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr j) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_other_inl_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_other_inl_0 {i j : Fin d} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr j) (Sum.inl 0) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_self_inr_other
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_self_inr_other {i j : Fin d} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr i) (Sum.inr j) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_other_inr_self
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_other_inr_self {i j : Fin d} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr j) (Sum.inr i) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_other_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_other_inr {i j k : Fin d} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr j) (Sum.inr k) = if j = k then 1 else 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_inr_inr_other
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_inr_inr_other {i j k : Fin d} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (boost i β hβ).1 (Sum.inr k) (Sum.inr j) = if j = k then 1 else 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inl_0_inr_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inl_0_inr_succ {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : Fin d) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr i.succ) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_succ_inl_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_succ_inl_0{d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : Fin d) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr i.succ) (Sum.inl 0) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inl_0_inr_nat_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inl_0_inr_nat_succ {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : ℕ) (h : i + 1 < d + 1) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr ⟨i + 1, h⟩) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_nat_succ_inl_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_nat_succ_inl_0 {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : ℕ) (h : i + 1 < d + 1) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr ⟨i + 1, h⟩) (Sum.inl 0) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_0_inr_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_0_inr_succ {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : Fin d) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr 0) (Sum.inr i.succ) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_succ_inr_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_succ_inr_0 {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : Fin d) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr i.succ) (Sum.inr 0) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_0_inr_nat_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_0_inr_nat_succ {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : ℕ) (h : i + 1 < d + 1) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr 0) (Sum.inr ⟨i + 1, h⟩) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_nat_succ_inr_0
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_nat_succ_inr_0 {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i : ℕ) (h : i + 1 < d + 1) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr ⟨i + 1, h⟩) (Sum.inr 0) = 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.boost_zero_inr_succ_inr_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_inr_succ_inr_succ {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (i1 i2 : Fin d) :
    (boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ).1 (Sum.inr i1.succ) (Sum.inr i2.succ) =
    if i1 = i2 then 1 else 0

modules.title: Generalized Boosts
modules.doc:
This module defines a generalization of the traditional boosts.
They are define given two velocities `u` and `v`, as an input an take
the velocity `u` to the velocity `v`.

We show that these generalised boosts are Lorentz transformations,
and furthermore sit in the restricted Lorentz group.

A boost is the special case of a generalised boost when `u = basis 0`.

## References

* The main argument follows: Guillem Cobos, The Lorentz Group, 2015:
  https://diposit.ub.edu/dspace/bitstream/2445/68763/2/memoria.pdf. [ref: cobos_2015_lorentz_group]

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁
declarations.doc: An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost.
declarations.statement: def genBoostAux₁ (u v : Velocity d) : Vector d →ₗ[ℝ] Vector d

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₂
declarations.doc: An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost.
declarations.statement: def genBoostAux₂ (u v : Velocity d) : Vector d →ₗ[ℝ] Vector d

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₂_self
declarations.statement: lemma genBoostAux₂_self (u : Velocity d) : genBoostAux₂ u u = - genBoostAux₁ u u

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁_apply_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₁_apply_basis (u v : Velocity d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (genBoostAux₁ u v) (Vector.basis μ) = (2 * η μ μ * u.1 μ) • v

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₂_apply_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₂_apply_basis (u v : Velocity d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (genBoostAux₂ u v) (Vector.basis μ) =
    - (η μ μ * (u.1 μ + v.1 μ) / (1 + ⟪u.1, v.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1 + v.1)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁_basis_minkowskiProduct
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₁_basis_minkowskiProduct (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ⟪genBoostAux₁ u v (Vector.basis μ), genBoostAux₁ u v (Vector.basis ν)⟫ₘ =
    4 * η μ μ * η ν ν * u.1 μ * u.1 ν

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁_toMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₁_toMatrix_apply (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (LinearMap.toMatrix Vector.basis Vector.basis (genBoostAux₁ u v)) μ ν =
    η ν ν * (2 * u.1 ν * v.1 μ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₂_basis_minkowskiProduct
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₂_basis_minkowskiProduct (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ⟪genBoostAux₂ u v (Vector.basis μ), genBoostAux₂ u v (Vector.basis ν)⟫ₘ =
    2 * η μ μ * η ν ν * (u.1 μ + v.1 μ) * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν)
    * (1 + ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ)⁻¹

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁_basis_genBoostAux₂_minkowskiProduct
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₁_basis_genBoostAux₂_minkowskiProduct (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ⟪genBoostAux₁ u v (Vector.basis μ), genBoostAux₂ u v (Vector.basis ν)⟫ₘ =
    - 2 * η μ μ * η ν ν * u.1 μ * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₂_toMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₂_toMatrix_apply (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (LinearMap.toMatrix Vector.basis Vector.basis (genBoostAux₂ u v)) μ ν =
      η ν ν * (- (u.1 μ + v.1 μ) * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν)
      / (1 + ⟪u.1, v.1⟫ₘ))

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁_add_genBoostAux₂_minkowskiProduct
declarations.statement:
lemma genBoostAux₁_add_genBoostAux₂_minkowskiProduct (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ⟪genBoostAux₁ u v (Vector.basis μ) + genBoostAux₂ u v (Vector.basis μ),
    genBoostAux₁ u v (Vector.basis ν) + genBoostAux₂ u v (Vector.basis ν)⟫ₘ =
    2 * η μ μ * η ν ν * (- u.1 μ * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν)
      - u.1 ν * (u.1 μ + v.1 μ)
      + (u.1 μ + v.1 μ) * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν) * (1 + ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ)⁻¹ +
      2 * u.1 μ * u.1 ν)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.basis_minkowskiProduct_genBoostAux₁_add_genBoostAux₂
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_minkowskiProduct_genBoostAux₁_add_genBoostAux₂ (u v : Velocity d)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ⟪Vector.basis μ, genBoostAux₁ u v (Vector.basis ν) + genBoostAux₂ u v (Vector.basis ν)⟫ₘ =
    η μ μ * η ν ν * (2 * u.1 ν * v.1 μ
    - (u.1 μ + v.1 μ) * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν) * (1 + ⟪u.1, v.1⟫ₘ)⁻¹)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost
declarations.doc:
An generalised boost. This is a Lorentz transformation which takes the Lorentz velocity `u`
to `v`.
declarations.statement: def generalizedBoost (u v : Velocity d) : LorentzGroup d

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply (u v : Velocity d) (x : Vector d) :
    generalizedBoost u v • x = x + genBoostAux₁ u v x + genBoostAux₂ u v x

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply_mul_one_plus_contr
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply_mul_one_plus_contr (u v : Velocity d) (x : Vector d) :
    (1 + ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ) • generalizedBoost u v • x = (1 + ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ) • x +
    (2 * ⟪x, u⟫ₘ * (1 + ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ)) • v - ⟪x, u + v⟫ₘ • (u + v)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply_expand
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply_expand (u v : Velocity d) (x : Vector d) :
    generalizedBoost u v • x = x + (2 * ⟪x, u⟫ₘ) • v.1 -
      (⟪x, u + v⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1 + v.1)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply_fst (u v : Velocity d) :
    generalizedBoost u v • u.1 = v.1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply_snd (u v : Velocity d) :
    generalizedBoost u v • v.1 = (2 * ⟪u, v.1⟫ₘ) • ↑v - ↑u

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_self
declarations.doc:
This lemma states that for a given four-velocity `u`, the general boost
transformation `genBoost u u` is equal to the identity linear map `LinearMap.id`.
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_self (u : Velocity d) :
    generalizedBoost u u = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.genearlizedBoost_apply_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma genearlizedBoost_apply_basis (u v : Velocity d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    generalizedBoost u v • (Vector.basis μ) =
    Vector.basis μ + (2 * η μ μ * u.1 μ) • v - (η μ μ * (u.1 μ + v.1 μ)
      / (1 + ⟪u.1, v.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1 + v.1)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply_eq_minkowskiProduct
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply_eq_minkowskiProduct (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (generalizedBoost u v).1 μ ν = η μ μ * (⟪Vector.basis μ, Vector.basis ν⟫ₘ + 2 *
    ⟪Vector.basis ν, u⟫ₘ * ⟪Vector.basis μ, v.1⟫ₘ
    - ⟪Vector.basis μ, u + v⟫ₘ * ⟪Vector.basis ν, u + v⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u.1, v⟫ₘ))

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_apply_eq_toCoord
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_apply_eq_toCoord (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (generalizedBoost u v).1 μ ν = ((1 : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ) μ ν +
    2 * η ν ν * u.1 ν * v.1 μ
    - η ν ν * (u.1 μ + v.1 μ) * (u.1 ν + v.1 ν) / (1 + ⟪u.1, v⟫ₘ))

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_continuous_snd
declarations.statement: lemma generalizedBoost_continuous_snd (u : Velocity d) : Continuous (generalizedBoost u)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_continuous_fst
declarations.statement: lemma generalizedBoost_continuous_fst (u : Velocity d) : Continuous (generalizedBoost · u)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.id_joined_generalizedBoost
declarations.statement: lemma id_joined_generalizedBoost (u v : Velocity d) : Joined 1 (generalizedBoost u v)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_in_connected_component_of_id
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_in_connected_component_of_id (u v : Velocity d) :
    generalizedBoost u v ∈ connectedComponent 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_isProper
declarations.statement: lemma generalizedBoost_isProper (u v : Velocity d) : IsProper (generalizedBoost u v)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_isOrthochronous
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_isOrthochronous (u v : Velocity d) :
    IsOrthochronous (generalizedBoost u v)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_mem_restricted
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_mem_restricted (u v : Velocity d) :
    generalizedBoost u v ∈ LorentzGroup.restricted d

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_inv
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_inv (u v : Velocity d) :
    (generalizedBoost u v)⁻¹ = generalizedBoost v u

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.generalizedBoost_timeComponent_eq
declarations.doc: The time component of a generalised boost.
declarations.statement:
lemma generalizedBoost_timeComponent_eq (u v : Velocity d) :
    (generalizedBoost u v).1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) = 1 +
    ‖u.1.timeComponent • v.1.spatialPart -
      v.1.timeComponent • u.1.spatialPart‖ ^ 2 / (1 + ⟪u.1, v.1⟫ₘ)

modules.title: The Orthochronous Lorentz Group
modules.doc:
We define the give a series of lemmas related to the orthochronous property of lorentz
matrices.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.IsOrthochronous
declarations.doc: A Lorentz transformation is `orthochronous` if its `0 0` element is non-negative.
declarations.statement: def IsOrthochronous : Prop

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_iff_toVector_timeComponet_nonneg
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation is `orthochronous` if and only if its first column is
future pointing.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_iff_toVector_timeComponet_nonneg :
    IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ 0 ≤ (toVector Λ).timeComponent

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_iff_transpose
declarations.doc: A Lorentz transformation is orthochronous if and only if its transpose is orthochronous.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_iff_transpose :
    IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ IsOrthochronous (transpose Λ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_inv_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_inv_iff {Λ : LorentzGroup d} :
    IsOrthochronous Λ⁻¹ ↔ IsOrthochronous Λ

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_iff_ge_one
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation is orthochronous if and only if its `0 0` element is greater
or equal to one.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_iff_ge_one :
    IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ 1 ≤ Λ.1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthochronoustoVelocity
declarations.doc:
The `Lorentz.Velocity` from `Lorentz.toVector` of a orthochronous lorentz
transformation.
declarations.statement:
def orthochronoustoVelocity {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (h : IsOrthochronous Λ) :
    Lorentz.Velocity d

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.not_isOrthochronous_iff_le_neg_one
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation is not orthochronous if and only if its `0 0` element is less than
or equal to minus one.
declarations.statement:
lemma not_isOrthochronous_iff_le_neg_one :
    ¬ IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ Λ.1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) ≤ -1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_iff_not_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_iff_not_neg :
    IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ ¬ IsOrthochronous (- Λ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.neg_isOrthochronous_iff_not
declarations.statement:
lemma neg_isOrthochronous_iff_not {Λ : LorentzGroup d} :
    IsOrthochronous (- Λ) ↔ ¬ IsOrthochronous Λ

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.not_isOrthochronous_iff_le_zero
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation is not orthochronous if and only if its `0 0` element is
non-positive.
declarations.statement: lemma not_isOrthochronous_iff_le_zero : ¬ IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ Λ.1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) ≤ 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.not_isOrthochronous_iff_toVector_timeComponet_nonpos
declarations.statement:
lemma not_isOrthochronous_iff_toVector_timeComponet_nonpos :
    ¬ IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ (toVector Λ).timeComponent ≤ 0

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.id_isOrthochronous
declarations.doc: The identity Lorentz transformation is orthochronous.
declarations.statement: lemma id_isOrthochronous : @IsOrthochronous d 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.timeCompCont
declarations.doc: The continuous map taking a Lorentz transformation to its `0 0` element.
declarations.statement: def timeCompCont : C(LorentzGroup d, ℝ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.stepFunction
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary function used in the definition of `orthchroMapReal`.
This function takes all elements of `ℝ` less than `-1` to `-1`,
all elements of `R` greater than `1` to `1` and preserves all other elements.
declarations.statement: def stepFunction : ℝ → ℝ

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.stepFunction_continuous
declarations.doc: The `stepFunction` is continuous.
declarations.statement: lemma stepFunction_continuous : Continuous stepFunction

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMapReal
declarations.doc:
The continuous map from `lorentzGroup` to `ℝ` wh
taking Orthochronous elements to `1` and non-orthochronous to `-1`.
declarations.statement: def orthchroMapReal : C(LorentzGroup d, ℝ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMapReal_on_IsOrthochronous
declarations.doc: A Lorentz transformation which is orthochronous maps under `orthchroMapReal` to `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthchroMapReal_on_IsOrthochronous {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (h : IsOrthochronous Λ) :
    orthchroMapReal Λ = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMapReal_on_not_IsOrthochronous
declarations.doc: A Lorentz transformation which is not-orthochronous maps under `orthchroMapReal` to `- 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthchroMapReal_on_not_IsOrthochronous {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (h : ¬ IsOrthochronous Λ) :
    orthchroMapReal Λ = - 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMapReal_minus_one_or_one
declarations.doc: Every Lorentz transformation maps under `orthchroMapReal` to either `1` or `-1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthchroMapReal_minus_one_or_one (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    orthchroMapReal Λ = -1 ∨ orthchroMapReal Λ = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMap
declarations.doc: A continuous map from `lorentzGroup` to `ℤ₂` whose kernel are the Orthochronous elements.
declarations.statement: def orthchroMap : C(LorentzGroup d, ℤ₂)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMap_IsOrthochronous
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation which is orthochronous maps under `orthchroMap` to `1`
in `ℤ₂` (the identity element).
declarations.statement:
lemma orthchroMap_IsOrthochronous {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (h : IsOrthochronous Λ) :
    orthchroMap Λ = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroMap_not_IsOrthochronous
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation which is not-orthochronous maps under `orthchroMap` to
the non-identity element of `ℤ₂`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthchroMap_not_IsOrthochronous {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (h : ¬ IsOrthochronous Λ) :
    orthchroMap Λ = Additive.toMul (1 : ZMod 2)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_mul
declarations.doc: The product of two orthochronous Lorentz transformations is orthochronous.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_mul {Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d} (h : IsOrthochronous Λ)
    (h' : IsOrthochronous Λ') : IsOrthochronous (Λ * Λ')

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_mul_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_mul_iff {Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d} :
    IsOrthochronous (Λ * Λ') ↔ (IsOrthochronous Λ = IsOrthochronous Λ')

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroRep
declarations.doc: The homomorphism from `LorentzGroup` to `ℤ₂`.
declarations.statement: def orthchroRep : LorentzGroup d →* ℤ₂

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.IsOrthochronous.iff_in_orthchroRep_ker
declarations.doc:
The orthochronous Lorentz transformations form the kernel of the homomorphism from
`LorentzGroup` to `ℤ₂`.
declarations.statement: lemma IsOrthochronous.iff_in_orthchroRep_ker : IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ Λ ∈ orthchroRep.ker

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.orthchroRep_inv_eq_self
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism from `LorentzGroup` to `ℤ₂` assigns the same value to any Lorentz
transformation and its inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma orthchroRep_inv_eq_self (Λ : LorentzGroup d) : orthchroRep Λ = orthchroRep Λ⁻¹

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_iff_of_orthchroMap_eq
declarations.doc:
Two Lorentz transformations are both orthochronous or both not orthochronous if they are mapped
to the same element via the homomorphism from `LorentzGroup` to `ℤ₂`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_iff_of_orthchroMap_eq {Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d}
    (h : orthchroMap Λ = orthchroMap Λ') : IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ IsOrthochronous Λ'

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.isOrthochronous_on_connected_component
declarations.doc:
Two Lorentz transformations which are in the same connected component are either both
orthochronous or both not orthochronous.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrthochronous_on_connected_component {Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d}
    (h : Λ' ∈ connectedComponent Λ) : IsOrthochronous Λ ↔ IsOrthochronous Λ'

modules.title: The Proper Lorentz Group
modules.doc:
The proper Lorentz group is the subgroup of the Lorentz group with determinant `1`.

We define the give a series of lemmas related to the determinant of the Lorentz group.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.det_eq_one_or_neg_one
declarations.doc: The determinant of a member of the Lorentz group is `1` or `-1`.
declarations.statement: lemma det_eq_one_or_neg_one (Λ : 𝓛 d) : Λ.1.det = 1 ∨ Λ.1.det = -1

declarations.doc: The instance of a topological space on `ℤ₂` corresponding to the discrete topology.
declarations.statement: instance : TopologicalSpace ℤ₂

declarations.doc: The topological space defined by `ℤ₂` is discrete.
declarations.statement: instance : DiscreteTopology ℤ₂

declarations.doc: The instance of a topological group on `ℤ₂` defined via the discrete topology.
declarations.statement: instance : IsTopologicalGroup ℤ₂

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.coeForℤ₂
declarations.doc: A continuous function from `({-1, 1} : Set ℝ)` to `ℤ₂`.
declarations.statement: def coeForℤ₂ : C(({-1, 1} : Set ℝ), ℤ₂)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detContinuous
declarations.doc: The continuous map taking a Lorentz matrix to its determinant.
declarations.statement: def detContinuous : C(𝓛 d, ℤ₂)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detContinuous_eq_one
declarations.statement:
lemma detContinuous_eq_one (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    detContinuous Λ = Additive.toMul 0 ↔ Λ.1.det = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detContinuous_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma detContinuous_eq_zero (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    detContinuous Λ = Additive.toMul (1 : ZMod 2) ↔ Λ.1.det = - 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detContinuous_eq_iff_det_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma detContinuous_eq_iff_det_eq (Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d) :
    detContinuous Λ = detContinuous Λ' ↔ Λ.1.det = Λ'.1.det

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detRep
declarations.doc: The representation taking a Lorentz matrix to its determinant.
declarations.statement: def detRep : 𝓛 d →* ℤ₂

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detRep_continuous
declarations.doc:
The representation of the Lorentz group defined by taking the determinant `detRep` is
continuous.
declarations.statement: lemma detRep_continuous : Continuous (@detRep d)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.det_on_connected_component
declarations.doc:
Two Lorentz transformations which are in the same connected component have the same
determinant.
declarations.statement:
lemma det_on_connected_component {Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d} (h : Λ' ∈ connectedComponent Λ) :
    Λ.1.det = Λ'.1.det

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.detRep_on_connected_component
declarations.doc:
Two Lorentz transformations which are in the same connected component have the same
image under `detRep`, the determinant representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma detRep_on_connected_component {Λ Λ' : LorentzGroup d} (h : Λ' ∈ connectedComponent Λ) :
    detRep Λ = detRep Λ'

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.det_of_joined
declarations.doc: Two Lorentz transformations which are joined by a path have the same determinant.

The main result of this module is the homeomorphism `toBoostRotation`
from the restricted Lorentz group to the product of Lorentz velocities and rotations.

modules.title: The Minkowski matrix
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The aim of this module is to define the Minkowski matrix `η` in `d+1` dimensions, and
prove properties thereof.

The Minkowski matrix is the real matrix of the form `diag(1, -1, -1, -1, ...)`,
It is related to the Minkowski metric on `ℝ^(d+1)`.

Related to the Minkowski matrix is the notion of the dual of a matrix with respect to
the Minkowski metric. This is defined as `η * Λᵀ * η`, where `Λ` is a real matrix.
This will be used to help define the Lorentz group in later files.

## ii. Key results

- `minkowskiMatrix` : The Minkowski matrix in `d+1` dimensions.
- `minkowskiMatrix.dual` : The dual of a matrix with respect to the Minkowski metric,
  defined to be `η * Λᵀ * η`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Minkowski Matrix
  - A.1. Basic equalities
  - A.2. Notation for the Minkowski matrix
  - A.3. Components of the Minkowski matrix
  - A.4. Squaring the Minkowski matrix
  - A.5. Symmetry properties of the Minkowski matrix
  - A.6. Determinant of the Minkowski matrix
  - A.7. Injective properties of multiplying diagonal components
  - A.8. Action of the Minkowski matrix on vectors
- B. The Minkowski dual
  - B.1. The dual on the identity
  - B.2. The dual swaps multiplication
  - B.3. The dual is an involution
  - B.4. The dual commutes with the transpose
  - B.5. The dual preserves the Minkowski matrix
  - B.6. The dual preserves the determinants
  - B.7. Components of the dual

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The Minkowski Matrix

We first define the Minkowski matrix in `d+1` dimensions, and prove some basic properties.

### A.1. Basic equalities

We show some basic equalities for the Minkowski matrix.
In particular, we show it can be expressed as a block matrix.

### A.2. Notation for the Minkowski matrix

We define the notation `η` for the Minkowski matrix, which can be used when the namespace
`minkowskiMatrix` is opened.

### A.3. Components of the Minkowski matrix

We prove some simple properties related to the components of the Minkowski matrix.

### A.4. Squaring the Minkowski matrix

we show that the Minkowski matrix is self-inverting, i.e. `η * η = 1`,
as well as other properties related to squaring the Minkowski matrix.

### A.5. Symmetry properties of the Minkowski matrix

The Minkowski matrix is symmetric, due to it being diagonal.

### A.6. Determinant of the Minkowski matrix

We show the determinant of the Minkowski matrix is equal to `(-1)^d` where
`d` is the number of spatial dimensions.

### A.7. Injective properties of multiplying diagonal components

If `x` and `y` are reals then since `η μ μ` is non-zero for any `μ`, the equation
`η μ μ * x = η μ μ * y` implies `x = y`. We prove this as a lemma.
This is a useful part of the API but is not used often.

### A.8. Action of the Minkowski matrix on vectors

We show properties of the action of the Minkowski matrix on vectors.

## B. The Minkowski dual

Given a real matrix `Λ`, we define the dual of `Λ` with respect to the Minkowski metric
to be `η * Λᵀ * η`.

The ultimate idea is that for the Minkowski inner product
`⟪Λ x, y⟫ = ⟪x, dual Λ y⟫` for all vectors `x` and `y`.

An element `Λ` is in the Lorentz group if and only if `dual Λ = Λ⁻¹`. This will not be
shown in this module.

This notion of a dual is not quite a homomorphism because it reverses the order of multiplication.

### B.1. The dual on the identity

We show that the dual of the identity matrix is the identity matrix.

### B.2. The dual swaps multiplication

We show that the dual swaps multiplication, i.e. `dual (Λ * Λ') = dual Λ' * dual Λ`.

### B.3. The dual is an involution

We show that the dual is an involution, i.e. `dual (dual Λ) = Λ`.
### B.4. The dual commutes with the transpose
### B.5. The dual preserves the Minkowski matrix
### B.6. The dual preserves the determinants

### B.7. Components of the dual

We show a number of properties related to the components of the duals.

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix
declarations.doc: The `d.succ`-dimensional real matrix of the form `diag(1, -1, -1, -1, ...)`.
declarations.statement: def minkowskiMatrix {d : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.as_diagonal
declarations.doc: The Minkowski matrix as a diagonal matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma as_diagonal : @minkowskiMatrix d = diagonal (Sum.elim 1 (-1))

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.as_block
declarations.doc: The Minkowski matrix as a block matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma as_block : minkowskiMatrix =
    Matrix.fromBlocks (1 : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) ℝ) 0 0 (-1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.inl_0_inl_0
declarations.doc: The `time-time` component of the Minkowski matrix is `1`.
declarations.statement: lemma inl_0_inl_0 : @minkowskiMatrix d (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) = 1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.inr_i_inr_i
declarations.doc: The space diagonal components of the Minkowski matrix are `-1`.
declarations.statement: lemma inr_i_inr_i (i : Fin d) : @minkowskiMatrix d (Sum.inr i) (Sum.inr i) = -1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.off_diag_zero
declarations.doc: The off diagonal elements of the Minkowski matrix are zero.
declarations.statement: lemma off_diag_zero {μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d} (h : μ ≠ ν) : η μ ν = 0

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.η_diag_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma η_diag_ne_zero {μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d} : η μ μ ≠ 0

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.vecMul_apply
declarations.doc:
Right multiplication of a row vector by the Minkowski matrix multiplies each component by
the corresponding diagonal sign.
declarations.statement:
lemma vecMul_apply (v : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) → ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (v ᵥ* minkowskiMatrix) μ = v μ * minkowskiMatrix μ μ

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.sq
declarations.doc: The Minkowski matrix is self-inverting.
declarations.statement: lemma sq : @minkowskiMatrix d * minkowskiMatrix = 1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.η_apply_mul_η_apply_diag
declarations.doc: Multiplying any element on the diagonal of the Minkowski matrix by itself gives `1`.
declarations.statement: lemma η_apply_mul_η_apply_diag (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) : η μ μ * η μ μ = 1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.η_apply_sq_eq_one
declarations.statement: lemma η_apply_sq_eq_one (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) : η μ μ ^ 2 = 1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.eq_transpose
declarations.doc: The Minkowski matrix is symmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_transpose : minkowskiMatrixᵀ = @minkowskiMatrix d

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.det_eq_neg_one_pow_d
declarations.doc:
The determinant of the Minkowski matrix is equal to `-1` to the power
of the number of spatial dimensions.
declarations.statement: lemma det_eq_neg_one_pow_d : (@minkowskiMatrix d).det = (- 1) ^ d

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.prod_diagonal
declarations.doc: The product of all diagonal entries of the Minkowski matrix is `(-1) ^ d`.
declarations.statement: lemma prod_diagonal : ∏ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d, minkowskiMatrix μ μ = (-1) ^ d

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.prod_diagonal_comp_of_injective
declarations.doc: Reindexing all diagonal entries injectively does not change their product.

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.mul_η_diag_eq_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_η_diag_eq_iff {μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d} {x y : ℝ} :
    η μ μ * x = η μ μ * y ↔ x = y

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.mulVec_inl_0
declarations.doc: The time components of a vector acted on by the Minkowski matrix remains unchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulVec_inl_0 (v : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) → ℝ) :
    (η *ᵥ v) (Sum.inl 0) = v (Sum.inl 0)

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.mulVec_inr_i
declarations.doc: The space components of a vector acted on by the Minkowski matrix swaps sign.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulVec_inr_i (v : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) → ℝ) (i : Fin d) :
    (η *ᵥ v) (Sum.inr i) = - v (Sum.inr i)

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual
declarations.doc:
The dual of a matrix with respect to the Minkowski metric.
A suitable name for this construction is the Minkowski dual.
declarations.statement: def dual : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_id
declarations.doc: The Minkowski dual of the identity is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma dual_id : @dual d 1 = 1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_mul
declarations.doc: The Minkowski dual swaps multiplications (acts contravariantly).
declarations.statement: lemma dual_mul : dual (Λ * Λ') = dual Λ' * dual Λ

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_dual
declarations.doc: The Minkowski dual is involutive (i.e. `dual (dual Λ)) = Λ`).
declarations.statement: lemma dual_dual : Function.Involutive (@dual d)

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_transpose
declarations.doc: The Minkowski dual commutes with the transpose.
declarations.statement: lemma dual_transpose : dual Λᵀ = (dual Λ)ᵀ

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_eta
declarations.doc: The Minkowski dual preserves the Minkowski matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma dual_eta : @dual d η = η

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.det_dual
declarations.doc: The Minkowski dual preserves determinants.
declarations.statement: lemma det_dual : (dual Λ).det = Λ.det

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_apply
declarations.doc:
Expansion of the components of the Minkowski dual in terms of the components
of the original matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_apply (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    dual Λ μ ν = η μ μ * Λ ν μ * η ν ν

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_apply_minkowskiMatrix
declarations.doc:
The components of the Minkowski dual of a matrix multiplied by the Minkowski matrix
in terms of the original matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_apply_minkowskiMatrix (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    dual Λ μ ν * η ν ν = η μ μ * Λ ν μ

modules.doc:
## Pauli matrices

The pauli matrices are defined ultimately through
- `pauliMatrix` which is a map `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ`.
  The notation `σ` can be used as short hand.

A tensorial structure is put on `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ` to allow the
use of index notation.

sections.text:
### Inversions

Lemmas related to the inversions of the Pauli matrices.

### Products

These lemmas try to put the terms in numerical order.
We skip `σ0` since it's just `1` anyway.

### Commutation relations

Lemmas related to the commutation relations of the Pauli matrices.

declarations.doc: The trace of `σ3` multiplied by `σ1` is equal to `0`.
declarations.statement: lemma σ3_σ1_trace : Matrix.trace (σ3 * σ1) = 0

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ3_σ2_trace
declarations.doc: The trace of `σ3` multiplied by `σ2` is equal to `0`.
declarations.statement: lemma σ3_σ2_trace : Matrix.trace (σ3 * σ2) = 0

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ3_σ3_trace
declarations.doc: The trace of `σ3` multiplied by `σ3` is equal to `2`.
declarations.statement: lemma σ3_σ3_trace : Matrix.trace (σ3 * σ3) = 2

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ1_σ2_commutator
declarations.statement: lemma σ1_σ2_commutator : σ1 * σ2 - σ2 * σ1 = (2 * I) • σ3

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ1_σ3_commutator
declarations.statement: lemma σ1_σ3_commutator : σ1 * σ3 - σ3 * σ1 = - (2 * I) • σ2

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ2_σ1_commutator
declarations.statement: lemma σ2_σ1_commutator : σ2 * σ1 - σ1 * σ2 = -(2 * I) • σ3

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ2_σ3_commutator
declarations.statement: lemma σ2_σ3_commutator : σ2 * σ3 - σ3 * σ2 = (2 * I) • σ1

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ3_σ1_commutator
declarations.statement: lemma σ3_σ1_commutator : σ3 * σ1 - σ1 * σ3 = (2 * I) • σ2

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.σ3_σ2_commutator
declarations.statement: lemma σ3_σ2_commutator : σ3 * σ2 - σ2 * σ3 = -(2 * I) • σ1

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix_anticommutator
declarations.doc: Pauli matrices satisfy `{σᵢ, σⱼ} = 2 δᵢⱼ I`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliMatrix_anticommutator (i j : Fin 3) :
    pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) +
      pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) =
        ((2 * kroneckerDelta i j : ℕ) : ℂ) •
          (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix
declarations.doc: The matrix `a · σ` associated to a real three-vector `a`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def vectorMatrix (a : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_anticommutator
declarations.doc:
The anticommutator of two Pauli vectors is twice their Euclidean dot product
times the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorMatrix_anticommutator (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix b + vectorMatrix b * vectorMatrix a =
      ((2 * (a ⬝ᵥ b) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_commutator
declarations.doc:
The commutator of two Pauli vectors is twice `i` times the Pauli vector
associated to their cross product.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorMatrix_commutator (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix b - vectorMatrix b * vectorMatrix a =
      (2 * Complex.I) • vectorMatrix (a ⨯₃ b)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix_commutator
declarations.doc:
Pauli matrices satisfy `[σᵢ, σⱼ] = 2i ∑ₖ εᵢⱼₖ σₖ`, with the right-handed Levi-Civita symbol
`ε₀₁₂ = 1` and the indices `0, 1, 2` labelling `x, y, z`. This is the index form of
`vectorMatrix_commutator`, obtained at the basis vectors `a = eᵢ`, `b = eⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliMatrix_commutator (i j : Fin 3) :
    pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) -
      pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) =
        (2 * I) • ∑ k : Fin 3, (leviCivitaSymbol ![i, j, k] : ℂ) • pauliMatrix (Sum.inr k)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_mul_vectorMatrix
declarations.doc:
Product formula for Pauli vectors:
`(a · σ)(b · σ) = (a · b) I + i (a × b) · σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorMatrix_mul_vectorMatrix (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix b =
      ((a ⬝ᵥ b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) +
        Complex.I • vectorMatrix (a ⨯₃ b)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorMatrix_sq
declarations.doc: The square of `a · σ` is `|a|² I`.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorMatrix_sq (a : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    vectorMatrix a * vectorMatrix a =
      (∑ i : Fin 3, a i ^ 2 : ℝ) • 1

modules.title: The Pauli matrices, interpreted as a Clifford algebra

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.form
declarations.doc: The euclidean norm as a quadratic form.
declarations.statement: protected noncomputable def form : QuadraticForm ℝ (Fin 3 → ℝ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.ofCliffordAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The injection from the Clifford algebra over `PauliMatrix.form` into the algebra generated by
the `σ` matrices.
declarations.statement:
def ofCliffordAlgebra :
    CliffordAlgebra PauliMatrix.form →ₐ[ℝ] Algebra.adjoin ℝ {σ1, σ2, σ3}

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.ofCliffordAlgebra_ι_single
declarations.doc: The generators of the Clifford algebra correspond to the elements `σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCliffordAlgebra_ι_single (i : Fin 3) (r : ℝ) :
    ofCliffordAlgebra (CliffordAlgebra.ι _ (Pi.single i r)) =
        r • ⟨![σ1, σ2, σ3] i, Algebra.subset_adjoin <| by fin_cases i <;> simp⟩

modules.doc: ## Interaction of Pauli matrices with self-adjoint matrices

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliMatrix_mul_selfAdjoint_re
declarations.doc: The trace of a pauli-matrix multiplied by a self-adjoint `2×2` matrix is real.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_pauliMatrix_mul_selfAdjoint_re (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    (Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix μ * A.1)).re = Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix μ * A.1)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.selfAdjoint_ext_complex
declarations.doc:
Two `2×2` self-adjoint matrices are equal if the (complex) traces of each matrix multiplied by
each of the Pauli-matrices are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma selfAdjoint_ext_complex {A B : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)}
    (h0 : Matrix.trace (σ0 * A.1) = Matrix.trace (σ0 * B.1))
    (h1 : Matrix.trace (σ1 * A.1) = Matrix.trace (σ1 * B.1))
    (h2 : Matrix.trace (σ2 * A.1) = Matrix.trace (σ2 * B.1))
    (h3 : Matrix.trace (σ3 * A.1) = Matrix.trace (σ3 * B.1)) : A = B

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.selfAdjoint_ext
declarations.doc:
Two `2×2` self-adjoint matrices are equal if the real traces of each matrix multiplied by
each of the Pauli-matrices are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma selfAdjoint_ext {A B : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)}
    (h0 : ((Matrix.trace (σ0 * A.1))).re = ((Matrix.trace (σ0 * B.1))).re)
    (h1 : ((Matrix.trace (σ1 * A.1))).re = ((Matrix.trace (σ1 * B.1))).re)
    (h2 : ((Matrix.trace (σ2 * A.1))).re = ((Matrix.trace (σ2 * B.1))).re)
    (h3 : ((Matrix.trace (σ3 * A.1))).re = ((Matrix.trace (σ3 * B.1))).re) :
    A = B

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary function which on `i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` returns the corresponding
Pauli matrix as a self-adjoint matrix.
declarations.statement:
def pauliSelfAdjoint (i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint_linearly_independent
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices are linearly independent.
declarations.statement: lemma pauliSelfAdjoint_linearly_independent : LinearIndependent ℝ pauliSelfAdjoint

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliMatrix_mul_pauliMatrix
declarations.doc: Pauli matrices are orthogonal with respect to the trace pairing: `tr(σ_μ σ_ν) = 2 δ_μν`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_pauliMatrix_mul_pauliMatrix (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix μ * pauliMatrix ν) = ((2 * kroneckerDelta μ ν : ℕ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliCoeff
declarations.doc: The four real Pauli coefficients of a self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrix.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pauliCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℝ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.sum_pauliCoeff
declarations.doc: Every self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrix is its Pauli decomposition.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    ∑ i, pauliCoeff A i • pauliSelfAdjoint i = A

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.eq_sum_pauli
declarations.doc: Every self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrix is a real linear combination of the Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_pauli
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    A = ∑ i, pauliCoeff A i • pauliSelfAdjoint i

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint_span
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices span all self-adjoint matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliSelfAdjoint_span :
    ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range pauliSelfAdjoint)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis
declarations.doc: The basis of `selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)` formed by Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
def pauliBasis :
    Basis (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ (selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ))

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.scalarCoeff
declarations.doc: The coefficient of the identity in the Pauli decomposition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def scalarCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) : ℝ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorCoeff
declarations.doc: The three spatial Pauli coefficients.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def vectorCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) : Fin 3 → ℝ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorPart
declarations.doc: The traceless Pauli-vector part `a · σ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def vectorPart
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliRadius
declarations.doc: The Euclidean length of the spatial Pauli coefficients.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pauliRadius
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) : ℝ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliRadius_sq
declarations.doc:
The Pauli radius is the square root of the squared Euclidean length of the
spatial Pauli coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliRadius_sq
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    pauliRadius A ^ 2 =
      ∑ i : Fin 3, vectorCoeff A i ^ 2

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliRadius_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliRadius_nonneg
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    0 ≤ pauliRadius A

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.matrix_eq_scalar_add_vector
declarations.doc: A self-adjoint matrix is its scalar part plus its Pauli-vector part.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_eq_scalar_add_vector
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    A.val = (scalarCoeff A : ℂ) • 1 + vectorPart A

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.trace_eq_two_mul_scalarCoeff
declarations.doc: The trace of a self-adjoint matrix is twice its scalar Pauli coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_eq_two_mul_scalarCoeff
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Matrix.trace A.1 = 2 * scalarCoeff A

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.trace_vectorPart
declarations.doc: The Pauli-vector part has zero trace.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_vectorPart
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    Matrix.trace (vectorPart A) = 0

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.vectorPart_sq
declarations.doc:
The square of the vector part of a self-adjoint matrix is its squared
Pauli radius times the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorPart_sq
    (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    vectorPart A * vectorPart A =
      (pauliRadius A ^ 2 : ℝ) • 1

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint'
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary function which on `i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` returns the corresponding
Pauli-matrix as a self-adjoint matrix with a minus sign for `Sum.inr _`.
declarations.statement: def pauliSelfAdjoint' (i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul
declarations.doc:
Trace orthogonality of the covariant Pauli basis:
`tr (σ'_a σ'_b) = 2 δ_{a b}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Matrix.trace ((pauliSelfAdjoint' a).1 * (pauliSelfAdjoint' b).1) =
      if a = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul_apply
declarations.doc:
The trace pairing of a covariant Pauli matrix with an arbitrary matrix, expressed through the
matrix entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_pauliSelfAdjoint'_mul_apply (l : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (N : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    Matrix.trace ((pauliSelfAdjoint' l).1 * N) =
      match l with
      | Sum.inl 0 => N 0 0 + N 1 1
      | Sum.inr 0 => -(N 0 1 + N 1 0)
      | Sum.inr 1 => -(Complex.I * (N 0 1 - N 1 0))
      | Sum.inr 2 => -(N 0 0 - N 1 1)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint'_linearly_independent
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices where `σi` are negated are linearly independent.
declarations.statement: lemma pauliSelfAdjoint'_linearly_independent : LinearIndependent ℝ pauliSelfAdjoint'

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliSelfAdjoint'_span
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices where `σi` are negated span all Self-adjoint matrices.
declarations.statement: lemma pauliSelfAdjoint'_span : ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range pauliSelfAdjoint')

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'
declarations.doc:
The basis of `selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)` formed by Pauli matrices
where the `1, 2, 3` pauli matrices are negated. These can be thought of as the
covariant Pauli-matrices.
declarations.statement: def pauliBasis' : Basis (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ (selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ))

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_decomp
declarations.doc: The decomposition of a self-adjoint matrix into the Pauli matrices (where `σi` are negated).
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliBasis'_decomp (M : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    M = (1/2 * (Matrix.trace (σ0 * M.1)).re) • pauliBasis' (Sum.inl 0)
    + (-1/2 * (Matrix.trace (σ1 * M.1)).re) • pauliBasis' (Sum.inr 0)
    + (-1/2 * (Matrix.trace (σ2 * M.1)).re) • pauliBasis' (Sum.inr 1)
    + (-1/2 * (Matrix.trace (σ3 * M.1)).re) • pauliBasis' (Sum.inr 2)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_repr_inl_0
declarations.doc:
The component of a self-adjoint matrix in the direction `σ0` under
the basis formed by the covariant Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliBasis'_repr_inl_0 (M : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    pauliBasis'.repr M (Sum.inl 0) = 1 / 2 * Matrix.trace (σ0 * M.1)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_repr_inr_0
declarations.doc:
The component of a self-adjoint matrix in the direction `-σ1` under
the basis formed by the covariant Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliBasis'_repr_inr_0 (M : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    pauliBasis'.repr M (Sum.inr 0) = - 1 / 2 * Matrix.trace (σ1 * M.1)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_repr_inr_1
declarations.doc:
The component of a self-adjoint matrix in the direction `-σ2` under
the basis formed by the covariant Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliBasis'_repr_inr_1 (M : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    pauliBasis'.repr M (Sum.inr 1) = - 1 / 2 * Matrix.trace (σ2 * M.1)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_repr_inr_2
declarations.doc:
The component of a self-adjoint matrix in the direction `-σ3` under
the basis formed by the covariant Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliBasis'_repr_inr_2 (M : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    pauliBasis'.repr M (Sum.inr 2) = - 1 / 2 * Matrix.trace (σ3 * M.1)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis_minkowskiMetric_pauliBasis'
declarations.doc:
The relationship between the basis `pauliBasis` of contravariant Pauli-matrices and the basis
`pauliBasis'` of covariant Pauli matrices is by multiplication by the Minkowski matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliBasis_minkowskiMetric_pauliBasis' (i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    pauliBasis i = minkowskiMatrix i i • pauliBasis' i

modules.title: Coordinate-axis rotations in `SL(2,ℂ)`
modules.doc:
This file defines chosen `SL(2,ℂ)` rotations carrying the `z`-axis to a selected coordinate axis.
The spatial-axis convention is `0 = x`, `1 = y`, and `2 = z`; consequently, the rotation associated
with axis `2` is the identity.

Conjugation by these rotations transports a matrix written in the diagonal `z`-axis basis to
the corresponding coordinate-axis basis. This provides the common change of basis used by
coordinate-axis boosts and later constructions based on diagonal representatives.

The main declarations are:

- `rotationZToAxis`, the indexed family of rotations;
- `rotationZToAxis_zero_apply` and its companions, their matrix entries;
- `rotationZToAxis_zero_mul_diagonal_mul_inv` and its companions, their action on a
  diagonal matrix.

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis
declarations.doc: The `SL(2,ℂ)` rotation carrying the `z`-axis to axis `i`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rotationZToAxis : Fin 3 → SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_zero_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the rotation carrying the `z`-axis to the `x`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_zero_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    (rotationZToAxis 0).1 j k =
      ((((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, -1; 1, 1]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_one_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the rotation carrying the `z`-axis to the `y`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_one_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    (rotationZToAxis 1).1 j k =
      ((((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, Complex.I; Complex.I, 1]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_two_apply
declarations.doc: The rotation carrying the `z`-axis to itself is the identity matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_two_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    (rotationZToAxis 2).1 j k = (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_zero_inv_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the inverse rotation from the `x`-axis to the `z`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_zero_inv_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    ((rotationZToAxis 0)⁻¹).1 j k =
      ((((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, 1; -1, 1]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_one_inv_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the inverse rotation from the `y`-axis to the `z`-axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_one_inv_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    ((rotationZToAxis 1)⁻¹).1 j k =
      ((((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, -Complex.I; -Complex.I, 1]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_two_inv_apply
declarations.doc: The inverse rotation from the `z`-axis to itself is the identity matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_two_inv_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    ((rotationZToAxis 2)⁻¹).1 j k = (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_zero_mul_diagonal_mul_inv
declarations.doc:
Conjugating `diag(a, b)` by the rotation to the `x`-axis expresses it in the `x`-axis
basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_zero_mul_diagonal_mul_inv (a b : ℂ) :
    (rotationZToAxis 0).1 * !![a, 0; 0, b] * ((rotationZToAxis 0)⁻¹).1 =
      !![(a + b) / 2, (a - b) / 2; (a - b) / 2, (a + b) / 2]

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_one_mul_diagonal_mul_inv
declarations.doc:
Conjugating `diag(a, b)` by the rotation to the `y`-axis expresses it in the `y`-axis
basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_one_mul_diagonal_mul_inv (a b : ℂ) :
    (rotationZToAxis 1).1 * !![a, 0; 0, b] * ((rotationZToAxis 1)⁻¹).1 =
      !![(a + b) / 2, -Complex.I * (a - b) / 2;
        Complex.I * (a - b) / 2, (a + b) / 2]

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationZToAxis_two_mul_diagonal_mul_inv
declarations.doc: Conjugating `diag(a, b)` by the identity rotation leaves it unchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationZToAxis_two_mul_diagonal_mul_inv (a b : ℂ) :
    (rotationZToAxis 2).1 * !![a, 0; 0, b] * ((rotationZToAxis 2)⁻¹).1 =
      !![a, 0; 0, b]

modules.title: The group SL(2, ℂ) and it's relation to the Lorentz group
modules.doc: The aim of this file is to give the relationship between `SL(2, ℂ)` and the Lorentz group.

sections.text:
## Some basic properties about SL(2, ℂ)

Possibly to be moved to mathlib at some point.

## Representation of SL(2, ℂ) on spacetime

Through the correspondence between spacetime and self-adjoint matrices,
we can define a representation a representation of `SL(2, ℂ)` on spacetime.

## Homomorphism to the restricted Lorentz group

The homomorphism `toLorentzGroup` restricts to a homomorphism to the restricted Lorentz group.
In this section we will define this homomorphism.

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.inverse_coe
declarations.statement: lemma inverse_coe (M : SL(2, ℂ)) : M.1⁻¹ = (M⁻¹).1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.transpose_coe
declarations.statement: lemma transpose_coe (M : SL(2, ℂ)) : M.1ᵀ = (M.transpose).1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap
declarations.doc:
Given an element `M ∈ SL(2, ℂ)` the linear map from `selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)` to
itself defined by `A ↦ M * A * Mᴴ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toSelfAdjointMap (M : SL(2, ℂ)) :
    selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) →ₗ[ℝ] selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toSelfAdjointMap_apply (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    toSelfAdjointMap M A = ⟨M.1 * A.1 * Matrix.conjTranspose M, by
        noncomm_ring [selfAdjoint.mem_iff, star_eq_conjTranspose,
        conjTranspose_mul, conjTranspose_conjTranspose,
        (star_eq_conjTranspose A.1).symm.trans $ selfAdjoint.mem_iff.mp A.2]⟩

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_apply_det
declarations.statement:
lemma toSelfAdjointMap_apply_det (M : SL(2, ℂ)) (A : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    det ((toSelfAdjointMap M) A).1 = det A.1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_apply_pauliBasis'_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma toSelfAdjointMap_apply_pauliBasis'_inl (M : SL(2, ℂ)) :
    toSelfAdjointMap M (PauliMatrix.pauliBasis' (Sum.inl 0)) =
    ((‖M.1 0 0‖ ^ 2 + ‖M.1 0 1‖ ^ 2 + ‖M.1 1 0‖ ^ 2 + ‖M.1 1 1‖ ^ 2) / 2) •
      PauliMatrix.pauliBasis' (Sum.inl 0) +
    (- ((M.1 0 1).re * (M.1 1 1).re + (M.1 0 1).im * (M.1 1 1).im +
      (M.1 0 0).im * (M.1 1 0).im + (M.1 0 0).re * (M.1 1 0).re)) •
        PauliMatrix.pauliBasis' (Sum.inr 0)
    + ((- (M.1 0 0).re * (M.1 1 0).im + ↑(M.1 1 0).re * (M.1 0 0).im
      - (M.1 0 1).re * (M.1 1 1).im + (M.1 0 1).im * (M.1 1 1).re)) •
        PauliMatrix.pauliBasis' (Sum.inr 1)
    + ((- ‖M.1 0 0‖ ^ 2 - ‖M.1 0 1‖ ^ 2 + ‖M.1 1 0‖ ^ 2 + ‖M.1 1 1‖ ^ 2) / 2) •
      PauliMatrix.pauliBasis' (Sum.inr 2)

declarations.doc:

`L(M)_{i j} = ½ tr (σ'_i · M σ'_j M†)`.

modules.title: Cayley–Klein parameters
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Two complex numbers `a b` with `‖a‖² + ‖b‖² = 1`, the Cayley–Klein parameters, give the unitary
element `!![a, -conj b; b, conj a]` of `SL(2, ℂ)`. Its image in the Lorentz group is a rotation,
whose matrix is written explicitly in terms of `a` and `b`.

## ii. Key results

- `cayleyKlein` : the element of `SL(2, ℂ)` with Cayley–Klein parameters `a b`.
- `cayleyKlein_mem_unitaryGroup` : a Cayley–Klein element is unitary.
- `toLorentzGroup_cayleyKlein_mem_rotations` : the image of a Cayley–Klein element is a
  rotation.
- `cayleyKleinRotation` : the Lorentz-group rotation of the Cayley–Klein parameters `a b`.
- `cayleyKleinRotation_inr_inr` : the spatial block of `cayleyKleinRotation a b h` is the
  matrix written explicitly in terms of `a` and `b`.
- `exists_cayleyKleinRotation_apply_two` : every unit vector is the image of the third axis
  under some Cayley–Klein rotation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Cayley–Klein element
- B. The Cayley–Klein rotation

## iv. References

* https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Cayley-KleinParameters.html

The element `!![a, -conj b; b, conj a]` of `SL(2, ℂ)`, given by its Cayley–Klein

The rotation of the Cayley–Klein parameters `a b`, as an element of the Lorentz rotation

modules.title: `SL(2, ℂ)` is a double cover of the restricted Lorentz group
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The homomorphism `toRestrictedLorentzGroup` from `SL(2, ℂ)` to the restricted Lorentz group is
surjective; together with the kernel `{1, -1}` (`toLorentzGroup_eq_one_iff`), this makes
`SL(2, ℂ)` a double cover. Rotations come from the unitary elements, written with
their Cayley–Klein parameters `a b`; the time axis is moved to any velocity by a lower
triangular element. The proof follows the boost and rotation decomposition
`LorentzGroup.exists_boost_mul_rotation`.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_unitary_toLorentzGroup_eq` : every rotation is the image of a unitary element.
- `toRestrictedLorentzGroup_surjective` : the homomorphism to the restricted Lorentz group is
  surjective.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Rotations
- B. Boosts and surjectivity

## iv. References

* B. Oblak, *From the Lorentz Group to the Celestial Sphere*, arXiv:1508.00920,
  Section 2.3.2.

declarations.statement:

    ∃ M : SL(2, ℂ), LorentzGroup.toVector (toLorentzGroup M) = u.1

modules.title: Extra lemmas regarding `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap`
modules.doc:
This file redefines `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap` by dropping the special linear condition for its
first argument `M`. Then, `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_det_one` is proved for `M` being upper
triangular.

## Main definitions

- `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap'`: definitionally equal to `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap` but `M`
is not required to be special linear.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_det_one'`: proves `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_det_one` with the
additional requirement that `M` be upper triangular. The general case is reduced to this special
case via `Matrix.schur_triangulation` in `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_det_one`.

sections.text:
## Showing `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap` has determinant 1

Since `Lorentz.ℍ₂` as a real vector space has the 4 Pauli matrices as basis, we know that its vector
representation consists of 4 real components. This makes the matrix representation of
`toSelfAdjointMap M` a 4-by-4 real matrix `F`. To make the computation of `F.det` manageable, the
following basis is used instead of the Pauli matrices to induce as many zeros as possible in `F`:
$$
E_0 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix},
E_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
E_2 = \sigma_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix},
E_3 = -\sigma_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & i \\ -i & 0 \end{bmatrix},
$$
Suppose that $M = \begin{bmatrix} x & □ \\ 0 & y \end{bmatrix}$ is upper triangular, the basis
$\{E_k\}_{k=0}^3$ induces the matrix representation
$$
F = \begin{bmatrix}
  \lvert x\rvert^2 & □ & □ & □ \\
  0 & \lvert y\rvert^2 & 0 & 0 \\
  0 & □ & \operatorname{Re}(x\bar{y}) & -\operatorname{Im}(x\bar{y}) \\
  0 & □ & \operatorname{Im}(x\bar{y}) & \operatorname{Re}(x\bar{y}) \\
\end{bmatrix}.
$$
If $xy = 1$, the Schur complement formula `Matrix.det_fromBlocks₂₂` yields
$$\begin{align}
\det F &=
\begin{vmatrix}
  \operatorname{Re}(x\bar{y}) & -\operatorname{Im}(x\bar{y}) \\
  \operatorname{Im}(x\bar{y}) & \operatorname{Re}(x\bar{y})
\end{vmatrix} \det\left(\begin{bmatrix} \lvert x\rvert^2 & □ \\ 0 & \lvert y\rvert^2 \end{bmatrix} -
  \begin{bmatrix} □ & □ \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
  \begin{bmatrix} □ & □ \\ □ & □ \end{bmatrix}
  \begin{bmatrix} 0 & □ \\ 0 & □ \end{bmatrix}
\right) \\ &=
\lvert x\bar{y}\rvert^2 \lvert x\rvert^2 \lvert y\rvert^2 = \lvert xy\rvert^4 = 1.
\end{align}$$
This concludes `Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_det_one'`. To get
`Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap_det_one`, triangulate the special linear matrix using
`Matrix.schur_triangulation`, and observe that `Matrix.schurTriangulation` preserves the determinant
which is 1.

modules.title: Twin Paradox
modules.doc:
The twin paradox corresponds to the following scenario:

Two twins start at the same point `startPoint` in spacetime.
Twin A travels at constant speed to the spacetime point `endPoint`,
whilst twin B makes a detour through the spacetime `twinBMid` and then to `endPoint`.

In this file, we assume that both twins travel at constant speed,
and that the acceleration of Twin B is instantaneous.

The conclusion of this scenario is that Twin A will be older than Twin B when they meet at
`endPoint`. This is something we show here with an explicit example.

The origin of the twin paradox dates back to Paul Langevin in 1911.

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox
declarations.doc: The twin paradox assuming instantaneous acceleration.
declarations.statement:
structure InstantaneousTwinParadox where
  /-- The starting point of both twins. -/
  startPoint : SpaceTime 3
  /-- The end point of both twins. -/
  endPoint : SpaceTime 3
  /-- The point twin B travels to between the start point and the end point. -/
  twinBMid : SpaceTime 3
  endPoint_causallyFollows_startPoint : causallyFollows startPoint endPoint
  twinBMid_causallyFollows_startPoint : causallyFollows startPoint twinBMid
  endPoint_causallyFollows_twinBMid : causallyFollows twinBMid endPoint

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.properTimeTwinA
declarations.doc:
The proper time experienced by twin A travelling at constant speed
from `T.startPoint` to `T.endPoint`.
declarations.statement: def properTimeTwinA : ℝ

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.properTimeTwinB
declarations.doc:
The proper time experienced by twin B travelling at constant speed
from `T.startPoint` to `T.twinBMid`, and then from `T.twinBMid`
to `T.endPoint`.
declarations.statement: def properTimeTwinB : ℝ

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.ageGap
declarations.doc: The proper time of twin A minus the proper time of twin B.
declarations.statement: def ageGap : ℝ

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.ageGap_eq
declarations.doc:
The age gap in terms of the two legs of Twin B, `u = twinBMid - startPoint` and
`v = endPoint - twinBMid`: `ageGap = √⟪u + v, u + v⟫ₘ - (√⟪u, u⟫ₘ + √⟪v, v⟫ₘ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ageGap_eq :
    T.ageGap = √⟪(T.twinBMid - T.startPoint) + (T.endPoint - T.twinBMid),
      (T.twinBMid - T.startPoint) + (T.endPoint - T.twinBMid)⟫ₘ
      - (√⟪T.twinBMid - T.startPoint, T.twinBMid - T.startPoint⟫ₘ
        + √⟪T.endPoint - T.twinBMid, T.endPoint - T.twinBMid⟫ₘ)

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.ageGap_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
The age gap vanishes if and only if the turning point of Twin B lies on the straight
worldline of Twin A between the start and end points: Twin B does not turn. This is the
equality case of the reverse triangle inequality (`sqrt_add_eq_iff_of_causallyFollows`,
`minkowskiProduct_eq_iff_of_causallyFollows`).
declarations.statement:
lemma ageGap_eq_zero_iff : T.ageGap = 0 ↔
    ∃ μ ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, T.twinBMid = T.startPoint + μ • (T.endPoint - T.startPoint)

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.ageGap_nonneg
declarations.doc:
In the twin paradox with instantaneous acceleration, Twin A is always at least as old as
Twin B: the age gap is nonnegative. This is the reverse triangle inequality of Minkowski space
(`sqrt_add_sqrt_le_sqrt_add_of_causallyFollows`) applied to the two legs of Twin B.
declarations.statement: lemma ageGap_nonneg : 0 ≤ T.ageGap

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.example1
declarations.doc:
The twin paradox in which:
- Twin A starts at `0` and travels at constant
  speed to `[15, 0, 0, 0]`.
- Twin B starts at `0` and travels at constant speed to
  `[7.5, 6, 0, 0]` and then at (different) constant speed to `[15, 0, 0, 0]`.
declarations.statement: def example1 : InstantaneousTwinParadox

declarations.statement: lemma example1_properTimeTwinB : example1.properTimeTwinB = 9

declarations.name: SpecialRelativity.InstantaneousTwinParadox.example1_ageGap
declarations.statement: lemma example1_ageGap : example1.ageGap = 6

declarations.doc: The example above has a nonzero age gap.
declarations.statement: lemma example1_ageGap_ne_zero : example1.ageGap ≠ 0

modules.title: The Speed of Light
modules.doc:
The speed of light in a vacuum, in the format of `Physlib/Units/Constants.lean`.

## i. Overview

The speed of light has the dimension `L T⁻¹`, and its value in SI units is exact. Section F adds
the instance of one and the speed of light as a dimensioned quantity.

## ii. Key results

- `SpeedOfLight` : The speed of light in a chosen but arbitrary system of units.
- `speedOfLight` : The speed of light in our world, `299792458 m s⁻¹`.
- `SpeedOfLight.toWithDim` : The speed of light as a quantity with the dimension of
  length over time.
- `SpeedOfLight.toWithDim_scaleUnit` : The map `toWithDim` commutes with changes of units.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The type
- B. Instances
- C. Positivity
- D. The dimension
- E. The value in our world
- F. Specific to the speed of light
  - F.1. The instance of one
  - F.2. As a dimensioned quantity

## iv. References

* The defining value of the speed of light. [ref: bipm_si_brochure_2019]

sections.text: ## E. The value in our world

## F. Specific to the speed of light

### F.1. The instance of one

We define the instance of one for `SpeedOfLight` to be the speed of light equal to `1`.
This is useful when we are working in units where the speed of light is equal to one.

The speed of light as a quantity carrying the dimension of length over time,
