modules.title: Tensors
modules.doc:
This module sets up the tensors used for index notation in Physlib.

Physics picture:
- Choose a symmetry group `G` (for example, the Lorentz group).
- Give each index kind a name called a *color* (encoded by a type `C`).
  In Lorentzian notation, a typical choice is two colors: `up` and `down`.
- For each color, choose a representation of `G`.
- Fix a basis for each color. This determines which values that index can take and
  lets us speak about tensor components explicitly.
- Specify a dual color for each color, telling us which index pairs can contract.
- For dual pairs, provide the contraction/unit/metric data used for contraction and
  for raising/lowering indices.

All of this structure is packaged as a `TensorSpecies`.

For `S : TensorSpecies` and a list of index colors `c : Fin n → C`:
- `Tensor S c` is the type of tensors with those indices.
- `Pure S c` is the type of pure tensors, i.e. tensors of the form
  `v₀ ⊗ₜ v₁ ⊗ₜ v₂ …`.
- `ComponentIdx S c` is the type of allowed component labels for those indices.

This file realizes `Tensor S c` as a `PiTensorProduct`, relates pure tensors to
their components, constructs the component basis, and supplies the inherited
finite-dimensional and module-topology instances. It also defines the natural
action of `G` on pure tensors and tensors, the associated permutation maps, and
the map from rank-zero tensors to the scalars `k`.

From this setup we get the usual index-notation operations in a uniform way:
contraction, raising/lowering, and permutation of indices.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor
declarations.doc:
The tensors associated with a list of indices of a given color
`c : Fin n → C`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev Tensor {n : ℕ} (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b)
  (c : Fin n → C) : Type

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure
declarations.doc:
The type of pure tensors associated to a list of indices `c : OverColor C`.
A pure tensor is a tensor which can be written in the form `v1 ⊗ₜ v2 ⊗ₜ v3 …`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Pure (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b) (c : Fin n → C) : Type

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.congr_right
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_right {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c)
    (i j : Fin n) (h : i = j) : LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by rw [h]) (p j) = p i

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.congr_mid
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_mid {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (c' : C) (p : Pure S c)
    (i j : Fin n) (h : i = j) (hi : c i = c') (hj : c j = c') :
    LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by rw [hi] : c i = c') (p i) =
    LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by rw [hj] : c j = c') (p j)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.map_mid_move_left
declarations.statement:
lemma map_mid_move_left {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin n1 → C} (p : Pure S c)
    (p' : Pure S c1) {c' : C}
    (i : Fin n) (j : Fin n1) (hi : c i = c') (hj : c1 j = c') :
    LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by rw [hi] : c i = c') (p i) =
    LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by rw [hj] : c1 j = c') (p' j)
    ↔ LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by rw [hi, hj] : c i = c1 j) (p i) =
    (p' j)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.toTensor
declarations.doc: The tensor corresponding to a pure tensor.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toTensor {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c) : S.Tensor c

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.toTensor_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toTensor_apply {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (p : Pure S c) :
    toTensor p = PiTensorProduct.tprod k p

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update
declarations.doc:
Given a list of indices `c` of `n` indices, a pure tensor `p`, an element `i : Fin n` and
a `x` in `V (c i)` then `update p i x` corresponds to `p` where
the `i`th part of `p` is replaced with `x`.

E.g. if `n = 2` and `p = v₀ ⊗ₜ v₁` then `update p 0 x = x ⊗ₜ v₁`.
declarations.statement:
def update {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)] (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin n)
    (x : V (c i)) : Pure S c

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update_eq_function_update
declarations.statement:
lemma update_eq_function_update {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)]
    (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin n)
    (x : V (c i)) : update p i x = Function.update p i x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update_same
declarations.statement:
lemma update_same {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)] (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin n)
    (x : V (c i)) : (update p i x) i = x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update_diff
declarations.statement:
lemma update_diff {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)] (p : Pure S c) (i j : Fin n)
    (x : V (c i)) (hij : i ≠ j) : (update p i x) j = p j

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update_succAbove_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma update_succAbove_apply {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin (n + 1))]
    (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin n) (x : V (c (i.succAbove j))) :
    update p (i.succAbove j) x i = p i

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.toTensor_update_add
declarations.statement:
lemma toTensor_update_add {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)] (p : Pure S c)
    (i : Fin n) (x y : V (c i)) :
    (update p i (x + y)).toTensor = (update p i x).toTensor + (update p i y).toTensor

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.toTensor_update_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma toTensor_update_smul {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)] (p : Pure S c)
    (i : Fin n) (r : k) (y : V (c i)) :
    (update p i (r • y)).toTensor = r • (update p i y).toTensor

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.drop
declarations.doc:
Given a list of indices `c` of length `n + 1`, a pure tensor `p` and an `i : Fin (n + 1)`, then
`drop p i` is the tensor `p` with it's `i`th part dropped.

For example, if `n = 2` and `p = v₀ ⊗ₜ v₁ ⊗ₜ v₂` then `drop p 1 = v₀ ⊗ₜ v₂`.
declarations.statement:
def drop {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    Pure S (c ∘ i.succAbove)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update_succAbove_drop
declarations.statement:
lemma update_succAbove_drop {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin (n + 1))]
    (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin (n + 1)) (k : Fin n) (x : V (c (i.succAbove k))) :
    (update p (i.succAbove k) x).drop i = (p.drop i).update k x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.update_drop_self
declarations.statement:
lemma update_drop_self {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin (n + 1))]
    (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin (n + 1)) (x : V (c i)) :
    (update p i x).drop i = p.drop i

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.component
declarations.doc:
Given an element `b` of `ComponentIdx c` and a pure tensor `p` then
`component p b` is the element of the ring `k` corresponding to
the component of `p` in the direction `b`.

For example, if `p = v ⊗ₜ w` and `b = ⟨0, 1⟩` then `component p b = v⁰ ⊗ₜ w¹`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def component {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) : k

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.component_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma component_eq {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c) (φ : ComponentIdx c) :
    p.component φ = ∏ i, (b (c i)).repr (p i) (φ i)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.component_eq_drop
declarations.statement:
lemma component_eq_drop {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin (n + 1))
    (φ : ComponentIdx c) :
    p.component φ = ((b (c i)).repr (p i) (φ i)) *
    ((drop p i).component (fun j => φ (i.succAbove j)))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.component_update_add
declarations.statement:
lemma component_update_add {n : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)]
    {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin n)
    (x y :V (c i)) (b : ComponentIdx c) :
    (update p i (x + y)).component b = (update p i x).component b +
    (update p i y).component b

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.component_update_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma component_update_smul {n : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq (Fin n)]
    {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c) (i : Fin n)
    (x : k) (y : V (c i)) (b : ComponentIdx c) :
    (update p i (x • y)).component b = x * (update p i y).component b

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.componentMap
declarations.doc:
The multilinear map taking pure tensors `p` to a map `ComponentIdx c → k` which when
evaluated returns the components of `p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentMap {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) :
    MultilinearMap k (fun i => V (c i)) (ComponentIdx (S := S) c → k)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.componentMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma componentMap_apply {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C)
    (p : Pure S c) : componentMap c p = p.component

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.basisVector
declarations.doc:
Given an component idx `b` in `ComponentIdx c`, `basisVector c b` is the pure tensor
formed by `S.basis (c i) (b i)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basisVector {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) : Pure S c

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.component_basisVector
declarations.statement:
lemma component_basisVector {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (b1 b2 : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    (basisVector c b1).component b2 = if b1 = b2 then 1 else 0

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.induction_on_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma induction_on_pure {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {P : S.Tensor c → Prop}
    (h : ∀ (p : Pure S c), P p.toTensor)
    (hsmul : ∀ (r : k) t, P t → P (r • t))
    (hadd : ∀ t1 t2, P t1 → P t2 → P (t1 + t2)) (t : S.Tensor c) : P t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.componentMap
declarations.doc: The linear map from tensors to its components.
declarations.statement: def componentMap {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] (ComponentIdx (S := S) c → k)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.componentMap_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma componentMap_pure {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C)
    (p : Pure S c) : componentMap c (p.toTensor) = Pure.componentMap c p

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.ofComponents
declarations.doc: The tensor created from it's components.
declarations.statement:
def ofComponents {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) :
    (ComponentIdx (S := S) c → k) →ₗ[k] S.Tensor c

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.componentMap_ofComponents
declarations.statement:
lemma componentMap_ofComponents {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (f : ComponentIdx c → k) :
    componentMap c (ofComponents (S := S) c f) = f

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.ofComponents_componentMap
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_componentMap {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    ofComponents c (componentMap c t) = t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.basis
declarations.doc: The basis of tensors.
declarations.statement: def basis {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) : Basis (ComponentIdx (S := S) c) k (S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.basis_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_apply {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    basis c φ = (Pure.basisVector c φ).toTensor

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.basis_repr_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_pure {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C)
    (p : Pure S c) :
    (basis c).repr p.toTensor = p.component

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.induction_on_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma induction_on_basis {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {P : S.Tensor c → Prop}
    (h : ∀ b, P (basis c b)) (hzero : P 0)
    (hsmul : ∀ (r : k) t, P t → P (r • t))
    (hadd : ∀ t1 t2, P t1 → P t2 → P (t1 + t2)) (t : S.Tensor c) : P t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.componentMap_eq_repr
declarations.doc:
`componentMap` is the basis representation `(basis c).repr` definitionally; this bridges the two
notations wherever a component computation meets a `repr` rewrite.
declarations.statement:
lemma componentMap_eq_repr {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (t : S.Tensor c)
    (ψ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) : componentMap c t ψ = (basis c).repr t ψ

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.componentMap_ext
declarations.doc: Two tensors with the same colour sequence are equal when all their components agree.
declarations.statement:
lemma componentMap_ext {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {t₁ t₂ : S.Tensor c}
    (h : ∀ b, componentMap c t₁ b = componentMap c t₂ b) : t₁ = t₂

instance {k : Type} [Field k] {C : Type} {G : Type} [Group G]
    {V : C → Type} [∀ c, AddCommGroup (V c)] [∀ c, Module k (V c)]
    {basisIdx : C → Type} [∀ c, Fintype (basisIdx c)] [∀ c, DecidableEq (basisIdx c)]
    {rep : (c : C) → Representation k G (V c)} {b : (c : C) → Basis (basisIdx c) k (V c)}
    (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b)
    {c : Fin n → C} : FiniteDimensional k (S.Tensor c)

noncomputable instance {k : Type} [RCLike k] {C : Type} {G : Type} [Group G]
    {V : C → Type} [∀ c, AddCommGroup (V c)] [∀ c, Module k (V c)]
    {basisIdx : C → Type} [∀ c, Fintype (basisIdx c)] [∀ c, DecidableEq (basisIdx c)]
    {rep : (c : C) → Representation k G (V c)} {b : (c : C) → Basis (basisIdx c) k (V c)}
    (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b)
    {c : Fin n → C} : TopologicalSpace (S.Tensor c)

instance {k : Type} [RCLike k] {C : Type} {G : Type} [Group G]
    {V : C → Type} [∀ c, AddCommGroup (V c)] [∀ c, Module k (V c)]
    {basisIdx : C → Type} [∀ c, Fintype (basisIdx c)] [∀ c, DecidableEq (basisIdx c)]
    {rep : (c : C) → Representation k G (V c)} {b : (c : C) → Basis (basisIdx c) k (V c)}
    (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b)
    {c : Fin n → C} : IsTopologicalAddGroup (S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.actionP
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance actionP : MulAction G (Pure S c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.actionP_eq
declarations.statement: lemma actionP_eq {g : G} {p : Pure S c} : g • p = fun i => rep (c i) g (p i)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.rep_cast
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_cast {g : G} {c c1 : C} (p : V c) (h : c = c1) :
    LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) h (rep c g p) = rep c1 g (LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) h p)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.actionP_cast
declarations.statement:
lemma actionP_cast {g : G} {p : Pure S c} (h : c = c1) :
    LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) h (g • p) = g • LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) h p

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.drop_actionP
declarations.statement:
lemma drop_actionP {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} {i : Fin (n + 1)} {p : Pure S c} (g : G) :
    (g • p).drop i = g • (p.drop i)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.instSMul
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance (priority := high + 1) instSMul : SMul G (S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_eq {g : G} {t : S.Tensor c} : g • t =
    PiTensorProduct.map (fun i => rep (c i) g) t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance (priority := high + 1) actionT : MulAction G (S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_pure {g : G} {p : Pure S c} :
    g • p.toTensor = Pure.toTensor (g • p)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_add
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_add {g : G} {t1 t2 : S.Tensor c} :
    g • (t1 + t2) = g • t1 + g • t2

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_smul {g : G} {r : k} {t : S.Tensor c} :
    g • (r • t) = r • (g • t)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_zero
declarations.statement: lemma actionT_zero {g : G} : g • (0 : S.Tensor c) = 0

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_neg {g : G} {t : S.Tensor c} :
    g • (-t) = -(g • t)
noncomputable instance (priority := high + 1) : DistribMulAction G (S.Tensor c)
instance : SMulCommClass k G (S.Tensor c)
instance : SMulCommClass G k (S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.permP
declarations.doc:
Given a permutation `σ : Fin m → Fin n` of indices satisfying `IsReindexing` through `h`,
and a pure tensor `p`, `permP σ h p` is the pure tensor permuted according to `σ`.

For example if `m = n = 2` and `σ = ![1, 0]`, and `p = v ⊗ₜ w` then
`permP σ _ p = w ⊗ₜ v`.
declarations.statement:
def Pure.permP {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}
    (σ : Fin m → Fin n) (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) (p : Pure S c) : Pure S c1

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.permP_basisVector
declarations.statement:
lemma Pure.permP_basisVector {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}
    (σ : Fin m → Fin n) (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    Pure.permP σ h (Pure.basisVector c φ) =
    Pure.basisVector c1 (fun i => basisIdxCongr (by simp [h.preserve_color]) (φ (σ i)))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.permP_equivariant
TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT
declarations.doc:
The reindexing of a tensor based on a map `σ : Fin m → Fin n` of indices
satisfying `IsReindexing`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def permT {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}
    (σ : Fin m → Fin n) (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] S.Tensor c1

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_pure
TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.permP_id_self
declarations.statement:
lemma Pure.permP_id_self {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (p : Pure S c) :
    Pure.permP (id : Fin n → Fin n) (by simp : IsReindexing c c id) p = p

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_id_self
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_id_self {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c) :
    permT (id : Fin n → Fin n) (by simp : IsReindexing c c id) t = t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_congr_eq_id
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_congr_eq_id {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c)
    (σ : Fin n → Fin n) (hσ : IsReindexing c c σ) (h : σ = id) :
    permT σ (hσ) t = t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_congr_eq_id'
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_congr_eq_id' {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t t1 : S.Tensor c)
    (σ : Fin n → Fin n) (hσ : IsReindexing c c σ) (h : σ = id) (ht : t = t1) :
    permT σ (hσ) t = t1

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_equivariant
TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.permP_congr
TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_congr
TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.permP_permP
declarations.statement:
lemma Pure.permP_permP {n m1 m2 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m1 → C} {c2 : Fin m2 → C}
    {σ : Fin m1 → Fin n} {σ2 : Fin m2 → Fin m1} (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ)
    (h2 : IsReindexing c1 c2 σ2) (p : Pure S c) :
    Pure.permP σ2 h2 (Pure.permP σ h p) = Pure.permP (σ ∘ σ2) (h.comp h2) p

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_permT
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_permT {n m1 m2 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m1 → C} {c2 : Fin m2 → C}
    {σ : Fin m1 → Fin n} {σ2 : Fin m2 → Fin m1} (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ)
    (h2 : IsReindexing c1 c2 σ2) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    permT σ2 h2 (permT σ h t) = permT (σ ∘ σ2) (h.comp h2) t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_basis_repr_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_basis_repr_symm_apply {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}
    {σ : Fin m → Fin n} (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) (t : S.Tensor c)
    (φ : ComponentIdx c1) :
    (basis c1).repr (permT σ h t) φ =
    (basis c).repr t (fun i =>
      basisIdxCongr (by simp [IsReindexing.inv_perserve_color]) (φ (h.inv σ i)))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_basis_repr_of_id
declarations.doc: A reindexing whose slot map is pointwise the identity only transports the labels.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_basis_repr_of_id {n : ℕ} {c c1 : Fin n → C} {σ : Fin n → Fin n}
    (hσ : ∀ i, σ i = i) (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) (t : S.Tensor c)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c1) :
    (basis c1).repr (permT σ h t) φ =
    (basis c).repr t (fun i => basisIdxCongr (by rw [← h.2 i, hσ]) (φ i))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.permT_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_basis {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c1 : Fin m → C}
    {σ : Fin m → Fin n} (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ)
    (b : ComponentIdx c) :
    (permT σ h) (basis (S := S) c b) = basis c1 (fun i =>
      basisIdxCongr (by simp [h.2]) (b (σ i)))

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor
declarations.doc: The tensor structure for complex Lorentz tensors.
declarations.statement:
def complexLorentzTensor : TensorSpecies ℂ complexLorentzTensor.Color SL(2, ℂ)
    (fun c => match c with
      | Color.upL => Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl
      | Color.downL => Fermion.DualLeftHandedWeyl
      | Color.upR => Fermion.RightHandedWeyl
      | Color.downR => Fermion.DualRightHandedWeyl
      | Color.up => Lorentz.ComplexVector
      | Color.down => Lorentz.ComplexCoVector)
    basisIdx
    (fun c => match c with
      | Color.upL => Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.rep
      | Color.downL => Fermion.DualLeftHandedWeyl.rep
      | Color.upR => Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.rep
      | Color.downR => Fermion.DualRightHandedWeyl.rep
      | Color.up => Lorentz.ComplexVector.SL2CRep
      | Color.down => Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep)
    (fun c => match c with
    | Color.upL => Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.basis
    | Color.downL => Fermion.DualLeftHandedWeyl.basis
    | Color.upR => Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.basis
    | Color.downR => Fermion.DualRightHandedWeyl.basis
    | Color.up => Lorentz.ComplexVector.basis
    | Color.down => Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis)

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.contrPCoeff_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma contrPCoeff_basis {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color} (i j : Fin n)
    (hij : i ≠ j ∧ (complexLorentzTensor.τ (c i) = c j))
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) c) :
    Pure.contrPCoeff i j hij (Pure.basisVector c b) =
      if b i = basisIdxTauEquiv (c i) (basisIdxCongr hij.2.symm (b j)) then 1 else 0

modules.title: Complex Lorentz tensors with Gaussian integer components
modules.doc:
A complex Lorentz tensor whose components in the standard basis are Gaussian integers can be
written as `ofGaussianInt f` for a map `f` from component indices to `GaussianInt`. The
product, contraction and permutation of such tensors are again of this form, so identities
between them reduce to decidable equalities of Gaussian integers.

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.ofGaussianInt
declarations.doc:
A complex Lorentz tensor from a map
`(Π j, complexLorentzTensor.basisIdx (c j)) → GaussianInt`. All complex Lorentz tensors
with Gaussian integer coefficients with respect to the basis are of this form.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofGaussianInt {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color} :
    ((ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) c) → GaussianInt) →ₛₗ[GaussianInt.toComplex]
      ℂT(c)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.ofGaussianInt_basis_repr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofGaussianInt_basis_repr_apply {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    (f : (ComponentIdx c) → GaussianInt)
    (b :(ComponentIdx c)) :
  (Tensor.basis c).repr (ofGaussianInt f) b = GaussianInt.toComplex (f b)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.basis_eq_ofGaussianInt
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_eq_ofGaussianInt {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    (b : (ComponentIdx c)) :
    Tensor.basis c b
    = ofGaussianInt (fun b' => if b = b' then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.contr_basis_gaussianInt
declarations.statement:
lemma contr_basis_gaussianInt {c : complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    (i : complexLorentzTensor.basisIdx c)
    (j : complexLorentzTensor.basisIdx (complexLorentzTensor.τ c)) :
      ((complexLorentzTensor.contr c)
      (complexLorentzTensor.basis c i ⊗ₜ
      complexLorentzTensor.basis (complexLorentzTensor.τ c) j))
      = GaussianInt.toComplex (if i = basisIdxTauEquiv c j then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.prodT_ofGaussianInt_ofGaussianInt
declarations.statement:
lemma prodT_ofGaussianInt_ofGaussianInt {n n1 : ℕ} {c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    (f : (ComponentIdx c) → GaussianInt)
    {c1 : Fin n1 → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    (f1 : (ComponentIdx c1) → GaussianInt) :
    (prodT (ofGaussianInt f) (ofGaussianInt f1)) =
    ((ofGaussianInt (fun b => f (ComponentIdx.prod b).1 *
      f1 (ComponentIdx.prod b).2)))

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.contrT_ofGaussianInt_eq_sum_dropPairSection
complexLorentzTensor.contrT_ofGaussianInt
declarations.statement:
lemma contrT_ofGaussianInt {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} {h : i ≠ j ∧ complexLorentzTensor.τ (c i) = c j }
    (f : (ComponentIdx c) → GaussianInt) :
  (contrT n i j h (ofGaussianInt f)) = ((ofGaussianInt (fun b =>
    (∑ x : complexLorentzTensor.basisIdx (c i),
      f (DropPairSection.ofFinEquiv h.1 b
        (x, basisIdxCongr h.2 ((basisIdxTauEquiv (c i)).symm x)))))))

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.permT_ofGaussianInt
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_ofGaussianInt {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    {c1 : Fin m → complexLorentzTensor.Color}
    {σ : Fin m → Fin n} (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ)
    (f : ComponentIdx c → GaussianInt) :
    (permT σ h ((ofGaussianInt f))) =
    ((ofGaussianInt (fun b => f (fun i => basisIdxCongr
      (IsReindexing.inv_perserve_color h i) (b (h.inv σ i))))))

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.contr_unit
declarations.doc: Contraction on the right with `ComplexCoVector.unit` does nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.contr_unit (x : ComplexCoVector) :
    (TensorProduct.lid ℂ _ <|
    ComplexCoVector.contr.toLinearMap.rTensor _ <|
    (TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ _).symm <|
    x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (ComplexCoVector.unit (1 : ℂ))) = x

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contr_unit
declarations.doc: Contraction on the right with `ComplexVector.unit`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.contr_unit (x : ComplexVector) :
    (TensorProduct.lid ℂ _ <|
    ComplexVector.contr.toLinearMap.rTensor _ <|
    (TensorProduct.assoc ℂ _ _ _).symm <|
    x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (ComplexVector.unit (1 : ℂ))) = x

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.unit_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.unit_symm :
    ComplexCoVector.unit (1 : ℂ) = LinearMap.lTensor _ (LinearEquiv.refl _ _).toLinearMap
      (TensorProduct.comm ℂ _ _ (ComplexVector.unit (1 : ℂ)))

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.unit_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.unit_symm :
    (ComplexVector.unit (1 : ℂ)) = LinearMap.lTensor _ (LinearEquiv.refl _ _).toLinearMap
      (TensorProduct.comm ℂ _ _ (ComplexCoVector.unit (1 : ℂ)))

modules.title: Complex Lorentz vectors
modules.doc: We define complex Lorentz vectors in 4d space-time as representations of SL(2, C).

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.basis

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.basis_ρ_apply
declarations.statement:

lemma ComplexVector.basis_ρ_val (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : ComplexVector) :

    LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup M) *ᵥ v.val

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contr
declarations.doc:
The linear map from complexContr ⊗ complexCo to ℂ given by
summing over components of contravariant Lorentz vector and
covariant Lorentz vector in the
standard basis (i.e. the dot product).
In terms of index notation this is the contraction is ψⁱ φᵢ.
declarations.statement:
def ComplexVector.contr : (ComplexVector.SL2CRep.tprod ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contr_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.contr_tmul (ψ : ComplexVector) (φ : ComplexCoVector) :
    ComplexVector.contr (ψ ⊗ₜ φ) = ψ.toFin13ℂ ⬝ᵥ φ.toFin13ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contr_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.contr_basis (i j : Fin 4) :
    ComplexVector.contr (ComplexVector.basisFin4 i ⊗ₜ ComplexCoVector.basisFin4 j) =
    if i.1 = j.1 then (1 : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contr_basis'
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.contr_basis' (i j : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ComplexVector.contr (ComplexVector.basis i ⊗ₜ ComplexCoVector.basis j) =
    if i = j then (1 : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.contr
declarations.doc:
The linear map from complexCo ⊗ complexContr to ℂ given by
summing over components of covariant Lorentz vector and
contravariant Lorentz vector in the
standard basis (i.e. the dot product).
In terms of index notation this is the contraction is φᵢ ψⁱ.
declarations.statement:
def ComplexCoVector.contr : (ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep.tprod ComplexVector.SL2CRep).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ SL(2,ℂ) ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.contr_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.contr_tmul (φ : ComplexCoVector) (ψ : ComplexVector) :
    ComplexCoVector.contr (φ ⊗ₜ ψ) = φ.toFin13ℂ ⬝ᵥ ψ.toFin13ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.contr_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.contr_basis (i j : Fin 4) :
    ComplexCoVector.contr (ComplexCoVector.basisFin4 i ⊗ₜ ComplexVector.basisFin4 j) =
    if i.1 = j.1 then (1 : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.contr_basis'
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.contr_basis' (i j : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ComplexCoVector.contr (ComplexCoVector.basis i ⊗ₜ ComplexVector.basis j) =
    if i = j then (1 : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contr_tmul_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.contr_tmul_symm (φ : ComplexVector) (ψ : ComplexCoVector) :
    ComplexVector.contr (φ ⊗ₜ ψ) = ComplexCoVector.contr (ψ ⊗ₜ φ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.contr_tmul_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.contr_tmul_symm (φ : ComplexCoVector) (ψ : ComplexVector) :
    ComplexCoVector.contr (φ ⊗ₜ ψ) = ComplexVector.contr (ψ ⊗ₜ φ)

modules.doc:
## Modules associated with complex Lorentz vectors

We define the modules underlying complex Lorentz vectors.
These definitions are preludes to the definitions of
`Lorentz.complexContr` and `Lorentz.complexCo`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector
declarations.doc: The module for contravariant (up-index) complex Lorentz vectors.
declarations.statement:
structure ComplexVector where
  /-- The underlying value as a vector `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ`. -/
  val : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ

declarations.statement: def toFin13ℂFun : ComplexVector ≃ (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ)

declarations.doc:
The instance of `AddCommMonoid` on `ComplexVector` defined via its equivalence
with `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ`.
declarations.statement: instance : AddCommMonoid ComplexVector

declarations.doc:
The instance of `AddCommGroup` on `ComplexVector` defined via its equivalence

modules.title: Component indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

For a tensor species `S` and a list of colors `c : Fin n → C`, `ComponentIdx S c`
is the type of choices of a basis index for every color in `c`. For example, for a
tensor with colors `![.up, .down]`, an element of `ComponentIdx ![.up, .down]`
records one contravariant component index and one covariant component index.

This file contains the basic definition and congruence/cast API. Operations on
component indices induced by tensor products and contractions live in sibling files.

## ii. Key results

- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx` is the type of component indices for a tensor
  with a given list of colors.
- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.congr_right` relates entries whose positions are equal.
- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.cast` casts component indices along equivalent color maps.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic definitions

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx
declarations.doc:
Given a list of indices `c : Fin n → C`, the type `ComponentIdx c` is the type of
component indices of a tensor with those colors. For instance, if `c = ![.up, .down]`,
then an element of `ComponentIdx c` specifies one basis index for `.up` and one for
`.down`.

## i. Overview

This file contains the component-index API induced by dropping a pair of contracted
indices from a tensor.

The constructions here describe how component indices restrict along
`Fin.succSuccAbove`, and how the fiber of this restriction is equivalent to the two
component choices at the contracted positions.

## ii. Key results

- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.dropPair` restricts a component index by dropping
  two positions.
- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.DropPairSection` is the finite set of component
  indices mapping to a fixed restricted component index.
- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.DropPairSection.ofFinEquiv` identifies a
  `DropPairSection` with the two basis indices at the dropped positions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Dropping a pair
- B. Sections of the drop-pair map

modules.title: Component indices split at a single slot
modules.doc:
Component-index insertion and evaluation at a distinguished slot.

## i. Overview

`ComponentIdx c` is `∀ j, basisIdx (c j)`, so singling out one slot `i` splits a component index
into the label there and a component index for the remaining colours `c ∘ i.succAbove`. That is
mathlib's `Fin.insertNthEquiv` read at the family `fun j => basisIdx (c j)`, and it carries no
transports of its own.

This is the one-slot counterpart of the two-slot `DropPairSection.ofFinEquiv`, which singles out
the pair a contraction consumes, and of `ComponentIdx.prod`, which splits a concatenated colour
list into its two halves. Where those two are shaped by the operation that produced the colour
list, this one is shaped by a slot the caller names, which is what a general-rank component formula
needs: an operation acting at slot `i` leaves the other slots alone, and the formula should say so
at every rank rather than at the rank where the colour list happens to be a literal.

## ii. Key results

- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.insert` : the equivalence splitting a component index at a
    named slot.
- `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.insert_apply_self` and
    `TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.insert_apply_succAbove` : the two directions, slotwise.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The single-slot equivalence

## iv. References

There are no known references for the material in this module.

declarations.doc:
Splitting a component index at a named slot: the label at slot `i`, together with a component
index for the colours of the remaining slots. The dependent counterpart of `Fin.cons`, and the
single-slot analogue of the two-slot `DropPairSection.ofFinEquiv`.

def insert {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    basisIdx (c i) × ComponentIdx (S := S) (c ∘ i.succAbove) ≃ ComponentIdx (S := S) c

declarations.statement:
lemma insert_apply_self {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (i : Fin (n + 1))
    (x : basisIdx (c i) × ComponentIdx (S := S) (c ∘ i.succAbove)) :
    insert (S := S) i x i = x.1

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.ComponentIdx.insert_apply_succAbove
declarations.statement:
lemma insert_apply_succAbove {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → C} (i : Fin (n + 1))
    (x : basisIdx (c i) × ComponentIdx (S := S) (c ∘ i.succAbove)) (m : Fin n) :
    insert (S := S) i x (i.succAbove m) = x.2 m

modules.title: Conjugation structure on a tensor species
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Each index of a tensor carries a colour naming the representation it transforms in. A species
already has the variance dual `τ c`, the colour an index must meet to contract. Conjugation adds a
second involution, the conjugate colour `bar c`: the colour an index transforms in after complex
conjugation. A spinor index is the textbook example: complex conjugation sends a left-handed Weyl
spinor to a right-handed one, `(ψ_α)* = ψ̄_α̇`, so `bar` swaps the left- and right-handed colours
while fixing a real vector colour. Variance is untouched, so `bar` commutes with `τ`. In an N=1
chiral sector `bar` swaps chiral and anti-chiral indices.

`conjT` conjugates a tensor at the basis level: `star` each coordinate in the species basis and
place it at the conjugate colour. Reality and Hermiticity are stated through it: a tensor is real
when conjugation fixes it, and a metric is Hermitian when conjugating it swaps its two indices.

Conjugation is intrinsic species data, not a detachable add-on: a `ConjTensorSpecies` is a
`TensorSpecies` bundled (`extends`) with the conjugate-colour involution `bar` and the coherence
the recipe needs. `bar c` shares basis labels with `c` (`barIdx_eq`) and the contraction
coefficients survive `star` (`conj_contrComm`), which together make conjugation commute with
contraction. `conjT` is then `conj`-semilinear, involutive, and commutes with contraction; the
last makes reality and Hermiticity compatible with raising and lowering indices.

At the single-index level, `conjEquiv : V c ≃ₛₗ V (bar c)` realises this conjugation: it reads a
vector's coordinates, conjugates them with `ConjModule.starFinsupp`, and re-seats them at the
conjugate colour. It rests on the conjugate module `ConjModule`
(`Physlib.Mathematics.Modules.ConjModule`), the same vectors with the scalar action twisted by
conjugation (`i` acts as `−i`). Equipping the conjugate colours with such conjugate-module
carriers is what makes a metric `V c ⊗ V (bar c) → k` genuinely bilinear and `IsHermitian` an
honest conjugate-transpose.

## ii. Key results

- `ConjTensorSpecies` is a tensor species bundled with its conjugation.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.conjT` is the conjugation of a tensor.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_conjT` proves that conjugation is an involution.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_contrT` proves that conjugation commutes with contraction.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_eq_permT_iff` is the componentwise criterion for
  `conjT t = permT σ h t'`, the workhorse for proving reality and Hermiticity conditions.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.conjEquiv` is the single-slot conjugate-linear isomorphism `V c ≃ₛₗ V (bar c)`.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.IsHermitian` is the structural conjugate-transpose condition on a metric slot.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.toSquareMatrix` is the square component matrix of a rank-two tensor whose
  second colour is the conjugate of its first;
  `ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_eq_permT_swap_iff_toSquareMatrix_isHermitian` says that conjugation swaps
  the two slots of `M` exactly when this matrix is Hermitian.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.isContrDualMatching_bar` and `ConjTensorSpecies.dualIdxEquiv_bar` say that
  conjugation preserves which basis labels pair to `1` under contraction: the basis vectors of
  `bar c` and `τ (bar c)` with labels `i` and `j` contract to `1` exactly when those of `c` and
  `τ c` with the same labels do.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.conjSingleT` is the conjugation of a one-slot tensor, at the colour
  `![bar x]`; `ConjTensorSpecies.conjSingleT_basis` is its action on basis vectors.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.toSesqForm` is the sesquilinear form `s, t ↦ M(t, s̄)` of a rank-two tensor
  `M` with `bar (c 0) = c 1`. Hermiticity of `M` is Hermiticity of this form, Mathlib's
  `LinearMap.IsSymm`;
  `ConjTensorSpecies.isSymm_toSesqForm_iff_conjT_eq_permT` and
  `ConjTensorSpecies.isSymm_toSesqForm_iff_toSquareMatrix_isHermitian` are its tensor and matrix
  forms.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.isPosDef_toSesqForm_iff_toSquareMatrix_posDef`: `M` is positive-definite, i.e.
  its form is (`LinearMap.IsPosDef`), exactly when its square component matrix is `Matrix.PosDef`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The conjugation structure
- B. The conjugation of vectors
- C. Conjugation of tensors
- D. The involution law
- E. Commutation with contraction
- F. Hermitian pairings
- G. Dual bases under conjugation
- H. The sesquilinear form of a tensor
- I. Positive-definite tensors

sections.text:
## A. The conjugation structure

A `ConjTensorSpecies` bundles a `TensorSpecies` (`extends`) with the conjugation data.
Conjugation is defined at the basis level, where it is "`star` the components" (§B). Four of the
new fields are
bookkeeping on colours and index sets, trivial to supply per instance: `bar` (the conjugate-colour
involution), `bar_involution`, `bar_tau` (it commutes with `τ`), and `barIdx_eq` (a colour and its
conjugate share basis labels). The one substantive field is `conj_contrComm`, that the contraction
coefficients are unchanged by `star`; this is what makes conjugation commute with contraction (§D),
and for a real (δ) contraction it is `star δ = δ`.

## B. The conjugation of vectors

`conjEquiv` is the conjugate-linear isomorphism `V c ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] V (bar c)`: read off the
coordinates of a vector in the species basis, conjugate them (`star`), and re-seat them as the
coordinates at the conjugate colour (the index sets agree by `barIdx_eq`). It is the single-slot
shadow of `conjT`, packaged as a bundled equivalence so the Hermitian-metric layer can apply it to a
metric slot. Semilinearity is built in via the coordinate `star`; invertibility is `star`'s
involutivity together with `bar`'s.

## C. Conjugation of tensors

We define the conjugation map `conjT` through its action on components, record that it conjugates
components in place (`componentMap_conjT`), and show it is `conj`-semilinear and additive.

Conventions for the index notation in this file. Indices are written in slot order: in `M_{IJ̄}`,
`I` is the first slot (Lean slot `0`, colour `c 0`) and `J̄` the second (slot `1`, colour
`c 1 = bar (c 0)`). As a tensor, `g = g_{IJ̄} dφᴵ ⊗ dφ̄^J̄` takes a holomorphic vector in its first
slot and an antiholomorphic one in its second: `g(u, v̄) = g_{IJ̄} uᴵ v̄^J̄`. An index of a
conjugate colour carries a bar or a dot (`Ī`, `α̇`), and conjugation adds a bar to each index,
removing it from an index that already has one.

For chiral scalar fields `φᴵ`, the basis vectors are the derivatives `e_I = ∂/∂φᴵ`, and their
conjugates `ē_Ī = ∂/∂φ̄^Ī`. A Kähler metric is `g_{IJ̄} = ∂_I ∂_J̄ K = g(e_I, ē_J̄)`. Holomorphic
index first is the standard convention, used throughout; it is a choice, since
`∂_I ∂_J̄ K = ∂_J̄ ∂_I K` (Schwarz's theorem).

## D. The involution law

We prove `conjT_conjT`: conjugating a tensor twice returns it, up to the identity recolouring
`bar ∘ bar ∘ c = c`. The supporting lemmas reconcile the iterated basis-label casts.

## E. Commutation with contraction

We prove `conjT_contrT`: conjugation commutes with contracting two dual-coloured slots. The
contraction expands as a sum over the contracted index pair, and `conj_contrComm` matches the
conjugated coefficients to those on the `bar`-images.

## F. Hermitian pairings

A metric slot pairs a colour `c` with its conjugate `bar c`. `IsHermitian` is the structural form of
`g_{IJ̄} = conj g_{JĪ}`: conjugating and swapping the two slots through `conjEquiv` returns `g`'s
`star`. Because `V c` and `V (bar c)` are genuinely different modules this is the honest
conjugate-transpose, not a bare `g = g.flip`. The condition is fixed here as `IsHermitian`; a
downstream metric layer instantiates it for a concrete pairing.

A tensor `M_{IJ̄}` with one index and one conjugate index, such as a Kähler metric `g_{IJ̄}`, has
the matrix of components `(M_{IJ̄})` (`toSquareMatrix`), regarded as a square matrix over the labels
of `I`. Its entries are the components themselves. Lean needs this step because the labels of a
colour and of its conjugate are different types, identified by `barIdx_eq`, and Hermiticity,
positive-definiteness and the inverse are defined only for square matrices. `M` is Hermitian,
`(M_{IJ̄})* = M_{JĪ}`, exactly when this matrix is.

## G. Dual bases under conjugation

A lower index contracts with an upper one, and the bases are dual: `e_α` contracted with `e^β` gives
`δ_α^β`. This section shows that the conjugate bases are dual in the same way: `ē_α̇` contracted
with `ē^β̇` gives `δ_α̇^β̇`. For example, for a vector `vᴵ` and a covector `w_I`,
`(vᴵ w_I)* = v̄^Ī w̄_Ī`: the conjugate contraction pairs the same labels. This follows because
contraction commutes with conjugation (`conj_contrComm`).

## H. The sesquilinear form of a tensor

A tensor `g_{IJ̄}` with one index and one conjugate index, such as a Kähler metric, defines a
Hermitian form on vectors of one colour. By the slot conventions of §C, `g` takes a holomorphic
vector `u` in its first slot and an antiholomorphic vector in its second,
`g(u, v̄) = g_{IJ̄} uᴵ v̄^J̄`. To pair two vectors `s, t` of the same colour, one of them is
conjugated so that it fits the second slot.

Convention. We use Mathlib's sesquilinear forms, so that Mathlib's results on Hermitian and
positive-definite forms apply. A Mathlib form `⟨s, t⟩` is conjugate-linear in its left argument `s`.
So `s` is the vector that is conjugated: `s̄` goes into the second, barred slot of `g`, and `t` goes
unchanged into the first slot,

`⟨s, t⟩ = g(t, s̄) = g_{IJ̄} tᴵ s̄^J̄`.

The order of the arguments of `⟨s, t⟩` is thus opposite to the order of the slots of `g`. Physics
usually writes the form the other way round, `g_{IJ̄} uᴵ v̄^J̄`, conjugate-linear in its right
argument `v`. This does not change norms or Hermiticity: `⟨t, t⟩ = g_{IJ̄} tᴵ t̄^J̄` is the norm
squared of the kinetic term `g_{IJ̄} ∂φᴵ ∂φ̄^J̄`. It does change the matrix: on the basis
`e_I = ∂/∂φᴵ`, `⟨e_I, e_J⟩ = g(e_J, ē_I) = g_{JĪ}`, the transpose of `(g_{IJ̄})`.

`g` is Hermitian, `(g_{IJ̄})* = g_{JĪ}`, exactly when its form is (`LinearMap.IsSymm`,
`⟨s, t⟩* = ⟨t, s⟩`), and positive-definite, `⟨t, t⟩ > 0` for `t ≠ 0`, exactly when its form is
(`LinearMap.IsPosDef`). On a concrete species the colour conditions hold by `rfl`, so the form of
`g` on vectors of colour `x` is written `S.toSesqForm x g`.

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies
declarations.doc:
A tensor species bundled with a conjugation. Beyond the `TensorSpecies` it `extends`, it carries
the conjugate-colour involution `bar`, the index-set identification `barIdx_eq`, and the
contraction-coherence `conj_contrComm`. Also carries `bar_involution` and `bar_tau` (that `bar` is
involutive and commutes with the variance dual).
declarations.statement:
structure ConjTensorSpecies (k : Type) [CommRing k] [StarRing k] (C : Type) (G : Type) [Group G]
    (V : C → Type) [∀ c, AddCommGroup (V c)] [∀ c, Module k (V c)]
    (basisIdx : C → Type) [∀ c, Fintype (basisIdx c)] [∀ c, DecidableEq (basisIdx c)]
    (rep : (c : C) → Representation k G (V c)) (b : (c : C) → Basis (basisIdx c) k (V c))
    extends TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b where
  /-- The conjugate colour: the colour an index transforms in under complex conjugation; preserves
  variance (commutes with `τ`). -/
  bar : C → C
  /-- `bar` is an involution. -/
  bar_involution : Function.Involutive bar
  /-- `bar` commutes with the variance dual `τ`. -/
  bar_tau : ∀ c, bar (toTensorSpecies.τ c) = toTensorSpecies.τ (bar c)
  /-- Conjugation fixes the index set: the conjugate colour reuses the same basis labels.
  Conjugation conjugates components in an adapted basis; it never permutes labels, so the label
  sets of `c` and `bar c` coincide. -/
  barIdx_eq : ∀ c, basisIdx (bar c) = basisIdx c
  /-- Conjugation is equivariant: it preserves the action of the group. -/
  conj_basis_equivariant : ∀ (c : C) (g : G) (i j : basisIdx c),
      (b c).repr (rep c g (b c i)) j = star ((b (bar c)).repr
      (rep (bar c) g (b (bar c) (Equiv.cast (barIdx_eq c).symm i)))
      (Equiv.cast (barIdx_eq c).symm j))
  /-- Conjugation is compatible with contraction at the basis level: `star` of the contraction
  coefficient at colour `d` equals the coefficient at the conjugate colour `bar d`, with basis
  labels carried over by `barIdx_eq`. For a real (δ) contraction this is `star δ = δ`. -/
  conj_contrComm : ∀ (d : C) (x₁ : basisIdx d) (x₂ : basisIdx (toTensorSpecies.τ d)),
      star (toTensorSpecies.contr d (b d x₁ ⊗ₜ[k] b (toTensorSpecies.τ d) x₂))
        = toTensorSpecies.contr (bar d) (b (bar d) ((Equiv.cast (barIdx_eq d)).symm x₁) ⊗ₜ[k]
            b (toTensorSpecies.τ (bar d)) (basisIdxCongr (bar_tau d)
              ((Equiv.cast (barIdx_eq (toTensorSpecies.τ d))).symm x₂)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.bar_tau_of_bar
declarations.doc: If `bar a = d`, then `bar (τ d) = τ a`.
declarations.statement: lemma bar_tau_of_bar {a d : C} (hbar : S.bar a = d) : S.bar (S.τ d) = S.τ a

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjEquiv
declarations.doc:
The conjugate-linear slot isomorphism `V c ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] V (bar c)`: conjugate the
coordinates in the species basis and relabel to the conjugate colour via `barIdx_eq`.
declarations.statement: def conjEquiv {c : C} : V c ≃ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] V (S.bar c)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjEquiv_basis
declarations.doc:
`conjEquiv` on a basis vector: `b c i ↦ b (bar c) i` (relabelled through `barIdx_eq`), since the
basis coordinates of `b c i` are the indicator at `i` and `star` fixes `0` and `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjEquiv_basis {c : C} (i : basisIdx c) :
    S.conjEquiv (b c i) = b (S.bar c) (Equiv.cast (S.barIdx_eq c).symm i)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjEquiv_basis_repr
declarations.statement:
lemma conjEquiv_basis_repr {c : C} (v : V c) (φ : basisIdx (S.bar c)) :
    (b (S.bar c)).repr (S.conjEquiv v) φ
      = star ((b c).repr v (Equiv.cast (S.barIdx_eq c) φ))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjEquiv_equivariant
declarations.statement:
lemma conjEquiv_equivariant {c : C} (g : G) (v : V c) :
    S.conjEquiv (rep c g v) = rep (S.bar c) g (S.conjEquiv v)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.componentReindex
declarations.doc: Reindex component labels of `bar ∘ c` back to `c`, slotwise via the cast `barIdx_eq`.

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT
declarations.doc:
Conjugation of a tensor: conjugate the components and reindex the basis to the conjugate
colours.
declarations.statement:
def conjT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} : S.Tensor c →ₛₗ[starRingEnd k]
    S.Tensor (fun i => S.bar (c i))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_apply {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT t = ofComponents (fun i => S.bar (c i))
      (fun b => star (componentMap c t (S.componentReindex c b)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.componentMap_conjT
declarations.doc: Components of a conjugated tensor: the `star` of the original components, reindexed.
declarations.statement:
lemma componentMap_conjT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c)
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (fun i => S.bar (c i))) :
    componentMap (fun i => S.bar (c i)) (S.conjT t) b
      = star (componentMap c t (S.componentReindex c b))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toMatrix_conjT
declarations.doc:
Conjugating a rank-two tensor conjugates each component and bars both indices:
`(T̄)_{ĪJ̄} = (T_{IJ})*`, where barring a barred index removes the bar. For example, `ψ_α χ_β` goes
to `ψ̄_α̇ χ̄_β̇`, and a tensor `M_{IJ̄}` goes to `(M̄)_{ĪJ} = (M_{IJ̄})*`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_conjT {cs : Fin 2 → C} (t : S.Tensor cs) :
    toMatrix (S.conjT t) = ((toMatrix t).map star).submatrix
      (Equiv.cast (S.barIdx_eq (cs 0))) (Equiv.cast (S.barIdx_eq (cs 1)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_basis {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (i : ComponentIdx (S := S.toTensorSpecies) c) :
    S.conjT (basis c i) = basis (fun i => S.bar (c i)) ((S.componentReindex c).symm i)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjSingleT
declarations.doc:
Conjugation of a vector, `vᴵ ↦ v̄^Ī = (vᴵ)*`, landing at the conjugate colour. For example, a
left-handed Weyl spinor `ψ_α` goes to the right-handed `ψ̄_α̇`.
declarations.statement: def conjSingleT (x : C) : S.Tensor ![x] →ₛₗ[starRingEnd k] S.Tensor ![S.bar x]

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjSingleT_basis
declarations.doc:
Conjugation sends the basis vector `e_I` to `ē_Ī`, the basis vector of the conjugate colour with
the same label.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjSingleT_basis (x : C) (z : basisIdx x) :
    S.conjSingleT x (basis ![x] (ComponentIdx.single.symm z)) =
      basis ![S.bar x] (ComponentIdx.single.symm (cast (S.barIdx_eq x).symm z))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_pure {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (p : Tensor.Pure S.toTensorSpecies c) :
    S.conjT p.toTensor = Pure.toTensor (fun i => S.conjEquiv (p i))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_eq_permT_iff
declarations.doc:
Componentwise criterion for `conjT t = permT σ h t'`. The conjugate of `t` equals the
recolouring `permT σ h t'` exactly when, at every component, the `star`-conjugated reindexed
component of `t` matches the corresponding component of `permT σ h t'`. This packages the
`componentMap_conjT` expansion and the `repr`/`componentMap` bridge that the reality and Hermiticity
proofs downstream would otherwise repeat by hand; the caller is left only with the species-specific
permutation bookkeeping on the right-hand side.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_eq_permT_iff {n m : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {c' : Fin m → C}
    {σ : Fin n → Fin m} (h : IsReindexing c' (fun i => S.bar (c i)) σ)
    (t : S.Tensor c) (t' : S.Tensor c') :
    S.conjT t = permT σ h t' ↔
      ∀ φ : ComponentIdx (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (fun i => S.bar (c i)),
        star (componentMap c t (S.componentReindex c φ))
          = (Tensor.basis (fun i => S.bar (c i))).repr (permT σ h t') φ

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_equivariant
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_equivariant {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (g : G) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT (g • t) = g • S.conjT t

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isReindexing_bar_bar
declarations.doc:
The identity permutation satisfies `IsReindexing` from `c` to `bar ∘ bar ∘ c`, as `bar` is an
involution.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReindexing_bar_bar {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) :
    IsReindexing c (fun i => S.bar (S.bar (c i))) (id : Fin n → Fin n)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_conjT
declarations.doc:
Conjugation is an involution: conjugating twice returns the original tensor, up to the
`bar_involution` recolouring (the identity permutation `permT`).
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_conjT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT (S.conjT t)
      = permT id (S.isReindexing_bar_bar c) t

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.contrCond_bar
declarations.doc: Slots with dual colour in `c` have dual colour in `bar ∘ c`, as `bar` commutes with `τ`.

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_contrT
declarations.doc:
Conjugation commutes with contraction: conjugating a contracted tensor equals contracting the
conjugate on the `bar`-images of the same two slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_contrT {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (h : i ≠ j ∧ S.τ (c i) = c j) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT (contrT n i j h t)
      = contrT n i j (S.contrCond_bar h) (S.conjT t)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.IsHermitian
declarations.doc:
A pairing `g : V c ⊗ V (bar c) → k` is Hermitian when conjugating and swapping its two slots
via `conjEquiv` returns its `star`: `g (x ⊗ y) = star (g (conjEquiv.symm y ⊗ conjEquiv x))`.
declarations.statement: def IsHermitian {c : C} (g : V c ⊗[k] V (S.bar c) →ₗ[k] k) : Prop

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toSquareMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix `(M_{IJ̄})`, with entries unchanged, regarded as a square matrix over the labels of
`I`. Lean needs this step because the labels of a colour and of its conjugate are different types,
identified by `barIdx_eq`; only for a square matrix are Hermiticity, positive-definiteness and the
inverse defined. Convention: the unbarred index is the row and the barred index the column, entry
`(I, J)` being `M_{IJ̄}`, as physicists write the matrix. For a Kähler metric `g_{IJ̄}` it is the
usual matrix `(g_{IJ̄})`.
declarations.statement:
def toSquareMatrix {c : Fin 2 → C} (M : S.Tensor c) (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1 := by rfl) :
    Matrix (basisIdx (c 0)) (basisIdx (c 0)) k

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toSquareMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toSquareMatrix_apply {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (M : S.Tensor c)
    (i j : basisIdx (c 0)) :
    S.toSquareMatrix M hbar i j =
      toMatrix M i ((Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (c 0))).symm j)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toMatrix_eq_submatrix_toSquareMatrix
declarations.doc: `toMatrix M` is `toSquareMatrix M` with its columns labelled by `J̄` instead of `J`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_eq_submatrix_toSquareMatrix {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1)
    (M : S.Tensor c) :
    toMatrix M =
      (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).submatrix id (Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (c 0)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.conjT_eq_permT_swap_iff_toSquareMatrix_isHermitian
declarations.doc:
For `M_{IJ̄}`, the conjugate `(M̄)_{ĪJ} = (M_{IJ̄})*` and the swapped tensor `M_{JĪ}` have the
same index types, a barred index then an ordinary one. They are equal, `(M_{IJ̄})* = M_{JĪ}`,
exactly when the matrix `(M_{IJ̄})` is Hermitian. A Kähler metric satisfies this.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjT_eq_permT_swap_iff_toSquareMatrix_isHermitian {c : Fin 2 → C}
    (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    S.conjT M = permT ![1, 0] (IsReindexing.swap_of_eq hbar.symm
      ((congrArg S.bar hbar).symm.trans (S.bar_involution (c 0))).symm) M ↔
    (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).IsHermitian

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toMatrix_contractInnerT_eq_toSquareMatrix_mul
declarations.doc:
The matrix of `g_{IJ̄} t^{J̄K}` is the product of the square matrix `(g_{IJ̄})` and the matrix
`(t^{J̄K})`, with the rows of `(t^{J̄K})` labelled by `J`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_contractInnerT_eq_toSquareMatrix_mul [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies]
    {cs ds : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1) (h : S.τ (cs 1) = ds 0) (M : S.Tensor cs)
    (t : S.Tensor ds) :
    toMatrix (contractInnerT h M t) =
      S.toSquareMatrix M hbar * (toMatrix t).submatrix
        (dualIdxEquiv h ∘ (Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (cs 0))).symm)
        (id : basisIdx (ds 1) → _)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isContrDualMatching_bar
declarations.doc:
The conjugate bases are dual: if `e_α` contracted with `e^β` is `δ_α^β`, then `ē_α̇` contracted
with `ē^β̇` is `δ_α̇^β̇`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isContrDualMatching_bar [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies] (d : C) :
    IsContrDualMatching S.toTensorSpecies (S.bar d)
      ((basisIdxCongr (S.bar_tau d)).symm.trans ((Equiv.cast (S.barIdx_eq (S.τ d))).trans
        ((contrDualIdxEquiv S.toTensorSpecies d).trans (Equiv.cast (S.barIdx_eq d)).symm)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.dualIdxEquiv_bar
declarations.doc:
`dualIdxEquiv` sends a lower label `α` to the upper label `α` it contracts with to `1`.
Conjugation commutes with this: the dotted label `α̇` pairs with the dotted upper label `α̇`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualIdxEquiv_bar [Nontrivial k] [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies] {c1 c2 c3 : C}
    (h : S.τ c1 = c2) (h' : S.τ (S.bar c1) = c3) (hbar : S.bar c2 = c3) (x : basisIdx c1) :
    dualIdxEquiv h' (cast (S.barIdx_eq c1).symm x) =
      cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq c2).symm (dualIdxEquiv h x)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.dualIdxEquiv_bar_tau
declarations.doc:
Removing a bar and lowering an index commute on labels. From a label of the upper barred index
`J̄`, removing the bar and then lowering gives the same label of the lower index `J` as lowering and
then removing the bar.
```
upper J̄ (τ d)  → remove bar →  upper J (τ a)
      ↓ lower                        ↓ lower
lower J̄ (d)    → remove bar →  lower J (a)
```
The left-hand side of the statement goes across the top and down, the right-hand side down and
across the bottom.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualIdxEquiv_bar_tau [Nontrivial k] [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies] {a d : C}
    (hbar : S.bar a = d) (j : basisIdx (S.τ d)) :
    dualIdxEquiv (S.τ_τ_apply a)
        ((Equiv.cast (S.bar_tau_of_bar hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (S.τ d))).symm j) =
      Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq a) ((dualIdxEquiv (rfl : S.τ d = S.τ d)).symm j)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toSesqForm
declarations.doc:
The Hermitian form `⟨s, t⟩ = M(t, s̄) = M_{IJ̄} tᴵ s̄^J̄` of a tensor `M_{IJ̄}`, on vectors
`s, t`. Convention: as in Mathlib it is conjugate-linear in its left argument `s`; `s̄` fills the
second, barred slot of `M` and `t` the first, so the argument order is opposite to the slot order.
declarations.statement:
def toSesqForm (x : C) {c : Fin 2 → C} (M : S.Tensor c) (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1 := by rfl)
    (hx : S.τ x = c 0 := by rfl) : S.Tensor ![x] →ₗ⋆[k] S.Tensor ![x] →ₗ[k] k

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toMatrix₂_toSesqForm
declarations.doc:
Since the left argument of the form fills the second slot of `M` (`toSesqForm`),
`⟨e_I, e_J⟩ = M(e_J, ē_I) = M_{JĪ}`: the matrix of the form is the transpose of `(M_{IJ̄})`. For a
Kähler metric, `⟨∂_I, ∂_J⟩ = ∂_J ∂_Ī K = g_{JĪ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix₂_toSesqForm [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies] {x : C} {c : Fin 2 → C}
    (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (hx : S.τ x = c 0) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix₂ ((basis ![x]).reindex (ComponentIdx.single.trans (dualIdxEquiv hx)))
        ((basis ![x]).reindex (ComponentIdx.single.trans (dualIdxEquiv hx)))
        (S.toSesqForm x M hbar hx) = (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar)ᵀ

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isSymm_toSesqForm_iff_toSquareMatrix_isHermitian
declarations.doc: `⟨s, t⟩* = ⟨t, s⟩` for all `s, t` exactly when `(M_{IJ̄})* = M_{JĪ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSymm_toSesqForm_iff_toSquareMatrix_isHermitian [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies]
    {x : C} {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (hx : S.τ x = c 0) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    (S.toSesqForm x M hbar hx).IsSymm ↔ (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).IsHermitian

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isSymm_toSesqForm_iff_conjT_eq_permT
declarations.doc:
`⟨s, t⟩* = ⟨t, s⟩` for all `s, t` exactly when the conjugate of `M` equals `M` with its two
indices swapped, `(M_{IJ̄})* = M_{JĪ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSymm_toSesqForm_iff_conjT_eq_permT [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies]
    {x : C} {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (hx : S.τ x = c 0) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    (S.toSesqForm x M hbar hx).IsSymm ↔ S.conjT M = permT ![1, 0] (IsReindexing.swap_of_eq hbar.symm
      ((congrArg S.bar hbar).symm.trans (S.bar_involution (c 0))).symm) M

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isPosDef_toSesqForm_iff_toSquareMatrix_posDef
declarations.doc:
The form is positive-definite, Hermitian with `M_{IJ̄} tᴵ t̄^J̄ > 0` for every `t ≠ 0`, exactly
when the matrix `(M_{IJ̄})` is. A Kähler metric is positive-definite, which makes kinetic terms
positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPosDef_toSesqForm_iff_toSquareMatrix_posDef [HasContrDualBases S.toTensorSpecies]
    {x : C} {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (hx : S.τ x = c 0) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    (S.toSesqForm x M hbar hx).IsPosDef ↔ (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).PosDef

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isUnit_det_toSquareMatrix_of_isPosDef
declarations.doc: Over a field, the matrix `(M_{IJ̄})` of a positive-definite tensor is invertible.

modules.title: The inverse of a rank-two tensor
modules.doc:
The inverse `g^{J̄I}` of a tensor `g_{IJ̄}` with one index and one conjugate index, such as a
Hermitian metric, and the linear equivalence that contracts an index with `g`.

## i. Overview

The inverse of a tensor `g_{IJ̄}` is the tensor `g^{J̄I}`, with two upper indices, for which
`g_{IJ̄} g^{J̄K} = δ_I^K` and `g^{J̄I} g_{IK̄} = δ^J̄_K̄`.

The colours of the inverse are `![τ (c 1), τ (c 0)]`, so its barred index comes first, `g^{J̄I}`.
The usual `g^{IJ̄}` is the same tensor with its two indices swapped. With the barred index first,
`g_{IJ̄} g^{J̄K}` contracts adjacent indices, so the contraction laws need no reordering of the
inverse. The matrix `(g^{J̄I})`, with row `J` and column `I`, is the inverse of the matrix
`(g_{IJ̄})`. `inverseT` is defined by this matrix inversion and is zero when `(g_{IJ̄})` is not
invertible. The inverse of a Hermitian `g` is Hermitian (A), and the inverse of a
positive-definite `g` is positive-definite (B). When `(g_{IJ̄})` is invertible, the two contraction
laws hold and the inverse is unique (C). Then contracting an index with `g` is a linear
equivalence whose inverse contracts with `g^{J̄I}` (D).

## ii. Key results

- `ConjTensorSpecies.inverseT` is the inverse `g^{J̄I}` of a tensor `g_{IJ̄}`.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.toSquareMatrix_inverseT` says that the matrix `(g^{J̄I})` is `(g_{IJ̄})⁻¹`.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.isSymm_toSesqForm_inverseT` and
  `ConjTensorSpecies.isPosDef_toSesqForm_inverseT` say that the inverse of a Hermitian or
  positive-definite `g` is again Hermitian or positive-definite.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.contractInnerT_inverseT` and `ConjTensorSpecies.inverseT_contractInnerT` are
  the contraction laws `g_{IJ̄} g^{J̄K} = δ_I^K` and `g^{J̄I} g_{IK̄} = δ^J̄_K̄`.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.eq_inverseT_of_contractInnerT_eq_unitTensor` says that the inverse is unique.
- `ConjTensorSpecies.toConjDualAtIndex` contracts an index with `g`, as a linear equivalence
  whose inverse contracts with `g^{J̄I}`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The inverse
- B. Positive-definiteness
- C. The contraction laws
- D. Changing an index to its conjugate dual

## iv. References

- `Matrix.inv` and `Matrix.inv_def`, in `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/NonsingularInverse.lean`;
- `Matrix.PosDef.inv`, in `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean`.

sections.text:
## B. Positive-definiteness

Over a field, the matrix `(g_{IJ̄})` of a positive-definite `g` is invertible
(`isUnit_det_toSquareMatrix_of_isPosDef`), so `g` has a true inverse and the contraction laws of C
hold for it. That inverse is again positive-definite (`isPosDef_toSesqForm_inverseT`).

## C. The contraction laws

When the matrix `(g_{IJ̄})` is invertible, `g^{J̄I}` satisfies both contraction laws, and it is the
only tensor that satisfies the first. The unit tensor `δ` is defined over `RCLike` scalars, so
sections C and D use them.

## D. Changing an index to its conjugate dual

When the matrix `(g_{IJ̄})` is invertible, contracting an index `I` of a tensor with `g` changes it
to its conjugate dual `J̄`, and contracting with `g^{J̄I}` changes it back. The two contraction laws
of C make these mutually inverse. For a metric `g_{IJ̄}` with lower indices this lowers an index.
If `g` has upper indices, the same map raises one.

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.inverseT
declarations.doc:
The inverse `g^{J̄I}` of a tensor `g_{IJ̄}`. Its matrix, with row `J` and column `I`, is
`(g_{IJ̄})⁻¹`, and it is zero when `(g_{IJ̄})` is not invertible.
declarations.statement:
def inverseT {c : Fin 2 → C} (M : S.Tensor c) (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1 := by rfl) :
    S.Tensor ![S.τ (c 1), S.τ (c 0)]

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toMatrix_inverseT
declarations.doc:
The component `g^{J̄I}` is the entry `(J, I)` of `(g_{IJ̄})⁻¹`. The upper indices `J̄` and `I`
are labelled by the lower indices `J` and `I` they contract with.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_inverseT {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    toMatrix (S.inverseT M hbar) =
      (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar)⁻¹.submatrix
        (Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (c 0)) ∘
          (dualIdxEquiv (rfl : S.τ (c 1) = S.τ (c 1))).symm)
        (dualIdxEquiv (S.τ_τ_apply (c 0)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toSquareMatrix_inverseT
declarations.doc:
The matrix `(g^{J̄I})`, row `J` from the first, barred index and column `I` from the second, is
`(g_{IJ̄})⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSquareMatrix_inverseT {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1) (M : S.Tensor c) :
    S.toSquareMatrix (S.inverseT M hbar) (S.bar_tau_of_bar hbar) =
      (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar)⁻¹.submatrix
        (Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (c 0)) ∘
          (dualIdxEquiv (rfl : S.τ (c 1) = S.τ (c 1))).symm)
        (Equiv.cast (hbar ▸ S.barIdx_eq (c 0)) ∘
          (dualIdxEquiv (rfl : S.τ (c 1) = S.τ (c 1))).symm)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isSymm_toSesqForm_inverseT
declarations.doc:
The inverse of a Hermitian tensor is Hermitian. If `(g_{IJ̄})* = g_{JĪ}`, then
`(g^{J̄I})* = g^{ĪJ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSymm_toSesqForm_inverseT {x y : C} {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1)
    (hx : S.τ x = c 0) (hy : S.τ y = S.τ (c 1)) {M : S.Tensor c}
    (hM : (S.toSesqForm x M hbar hx).IsSymm) :
    (S.toSesqForm y (S.inverseT M hbar) (S.bar_tau_of_bar hbar) hy).IsSymm

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.isPosDef_toSesqForm_inverseT
declarations.doc:
The inverse of a positive-definite tensor is positive-definite, so `g^{J̄I} t_J̄ t̄_I > 0` for
every covector `t ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPosDef_toSesqForm_inverseT {x y : C} {c : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (c 0) = c 1)
    (hx : S.τ x = c 0) (hy : S.τ y = S.τ (c 1)) {M : S.Tensor c}
    (hM : (S.toSesqForm x M hbar hx).IsPosDef) :
    (S.toSesqForm y (S.inverseT M hbar) (S.bar_tau_of_bar hbar) hy).IsPosDef

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.contractInnerT_inverseT
declarations.doc:
If the matrix `(g_{IJ̄})` is invertible, `g_{IJ̄} g^{J̄K} = δ_I^K`. The first colour of the unit
tensor is renamed from `τ (τ (cs 0))` to `cs 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma contractInnerT_inverseT {cs : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1) (M : S.Tensor cs)
    (hM : IsUnit (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).det) :
    contractInnerT rfl M (S.inverseT M hbar) =
      permT id (IsReindexing.unitTensor_of_tau_eq (S.τ_τ_apply (cs 0)))
        (unitTensor (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (S.τ (cs 0)))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.inverseT_contractInnerT
declarations.doc: If the matrix `(g_{IJ̄})` is invertible, `g^{J̄I} g_{IK̄} = δ^J̄_K̄`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inverseT_contractInnerT {cs : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1) (M : S.Tensor cs)
    (hM : IsUnit (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).det) :
    contractInnerT (S.τ_τ_apply (cs 0)) (S.inverseT M hbar) M =
      unitTensor (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (cs 1)

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.eq_inverseT_of_contractInnerT_eq_unitTensor
declarations.doc:
If `(g_{IJ̄})` is invertible and `g_{IJ̄} t^{J̄K} = δ_I^K`, then `t` is the inverse
`g^{J̄K}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_inverseT_of_contractInnerT_eq_unitTensor {cs : Fin 2 → C} (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1)
    (M : S.Tensor cs) (hM : IsUnit (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).det)
    {t : S.Tensor ![S.τ (cs 1), S.τ (cs 0)]}
    (ht : contractInnerT rfl M t =
      permT id (IsReindexing.unitTensor_of_tau_eq (S.τ_τ_apply (cs 0)))
        (unitTensor (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (S.τ (cs 0)))) :
    t = S.inverseT M hbar

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toConjDualAtIndex
declarations.doc:
The linear equivalence that contracts slot `i` of a tensor with the first index of `M`, when
the matrix `(M_{IJ̄})` is invertible. Slot `i` changes from `τ (cs 0)` to its conjugate dual
`cs 1`, and the inverse contracts with `inverseT M`. For a metric `g_{IJ̄}` this lowers an
unbarred index to a barred one, `t_{J̄} = g_{IJ̄} t^I`.
declarations.statement:
def toConjDualAtIndex {cs : Fin 2 → C} (M : S.Tensor cs) (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1)
    (hM : IsUnit (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).det) :
    {n : ℕ} → {c : Fin n → C} → (i : Fin n) → (he : c i = S.τ (cs 0)) →
      S.Tensor c ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor (Function.update c i (cs 1))

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toConjDualAtIndex_apply
declarations.doc: `toConjDualAtIndex` is the contraction `crossToSlot` of slot `i` with the first index of `M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toConjDualAtIndex_apply {nA : ℕ} {c : Fin (nA + 1) → C} {cs : Fin 2 → C} (M : S.Tensor cs)
    (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1) (hM : IsUnit (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).det)
    (i : Fin (nA + 1)) (he : c i = S.τ (cs 0)) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.toConjDualAtIndex M hbar hM i he t =
      crossToSlot i 0 ((congrArg S.τ he).trans (S.τ_τ_apply (cs 0))) M t

declarations.name: ConjTensorSpecies.toConjDualAtIndex_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
The inverse of `toConjDualAtIndex` is the contraction `crossToSlotInv` of slot `i` with the
first index of `inverseT M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toConjDualAtIndex_symm_apply {nA : ℕ} {c : Fin (nA + 1) → C} {cs : Fin 2 → C}
    (M : S.Tensor cs) (hbar : S.bar (cs 0) = cs 1) (hM : IsUnit (S.toSquareMatrix M hbar).det)
    (i : Fin (nA + 1)) (he : c i = S.τ (cs 0)) (t : S.Tensor (Function.update c i (cs 1))) :
    (S.toConjDualAtIndex M hbar hM i he).symm t =
      crossToSlotInv (S := S.toTensorSpecies) (d := cs 1) i he rfl (S.inverseT M hbar) t

modules.title: Constructors of tensors.
modules.doc: There are a number of ways to construct explicit tensors.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.fromSingleP
declarations.doc: The equivalence between `V c` and `Pure S ![c]`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def Pure.fromSingleP {c : C} : V c ≃ₗ[k] Pure S ![c]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleT
declarations.doc: The equivalence between `V c` and `S.Tensor ![c]`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fromSingleT {c : C} : V c ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor ![c]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleT_symm_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma fromSingleT_symm_pure {c : C} (p : Pure S ![c]) :
    fromSingleT.symm p.toTensor = Pure.fromSingleP.symm p

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleT_eq_pureT
declarations.statement:
lemma fromSingleT_eq_pureT {c : C} (x : V c) :
    fromSingleT (S := S) x = Pure.toTensor (fun 0 => x : Pure S ![c])

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_fromSingleT
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_fromSingleT {c : C} (x : V c) (g : G) :
    g • fromSingleT (S := S) x = fromSingleT (rep c g x)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleT_map
declarations.statement:
lemma fromSingleT_map {c c1 : C}
    (h : c = c1) (x : V c) :
    fromSingleT (LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) h x) =
    permT id (by simp [h]) (fromSingleT (S := S) x)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.contrT_fromSingleT_fromSingleT
declarations.statement:
lemma contrT_fromSingleT_fromSingleT {c : C} (x : V c)
    (y : V (S.τ c)) :
    contrT (S := S) 0 0 1 (by simp; rfl) (prodT (fromSingleT x) (fromSingleT y)) =
    (S.contr c) (x ⊗ₜ[k] y) • (Pure.toTensor default)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT
declarations.doc:
The construction of a tensor with two indices from the tensor product
`V c1 ⊗[k] V c2 ` defined
categorically.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fromPairT {c1 c2 : C} :
    V c1 ⊗[k] V c2 →ₗ[k] S.Tensor ![c1, c2]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_tmul {c1 c2 : C} (x : V c1)
    (y : V c2) : fromPairT (x ⊗ₜ[k] y) =
    permT id (And.intro Function.bijective_id (fun i => by fin_cases i <;> rfl))
    (prodT (fromSingleT (S := S) x) (fromSingleT y))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_eq_pure
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_eq_pure {c1 c2 : C} (x : V c1) (y : V c2) :
    fromPairT (S := S) (x ⊗ₜ[k] y) = Pure.toTensor (fun | 0 => x | 1 => y)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_fromPairT
declarations.statement:
lemma actionT_fromPairT {c1 c2 : C}
    (x : V c1 ⊗[k]V c2)
    (g : G) :
    g • fromPairT (S := S) x = fromPairT (TensorProduct.map (rep c1 g)
      (rep c2 g) x)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_map_right
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_map_right {c1 c2 c2' : C} (h :c2 = c2')
    (x : V c1 ⊗[k] V c2) :
    fromPairT (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id
      (LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (M := V) h) x : _ ⊗[k] V c2') =
    permT id (by simp [h]) (fromPairT (S := S) x)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_comm
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_comm {c1 c2 : C}
    (x : V c1 ⊗[k] V c2) :
    fromPairT (TensorProduct.comm k _ _ x) =
    permT ![1, 0] (And.intro (by decide) (fun i => by fin_cases i <;> simp))
    (fromPairT (S := S) x)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleTContrFromPairT
declarations.doc: The contraction of tensors with one index with one with two indices defined categorically.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fromSingleTContrFromPairT {c c2 : C}
    (x : V c) (y : V (S.τ c) ⊗[k] V c2) : S.Tensor ![c2]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleTContrFromPairT_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma fromSingleTContrFromPairT_tmul {c c2 : C}
    (x : V c) (y1 : V (S.τ c)) (y2 : V c2) :
    fromSingleTContrFromPairT x (y1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2) =
    S.contr c (x ⊗ₜ[k] y1) • fromSingleT y2

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromSingleT_contr_fromPairT_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma fromSingleT_contr_fromPairT_tmul {c c2 : C}
    (x : V c) (y1 : V (S.τ c)) (y2 : V c2) :
    contrT 1 0 1 (by simp; rfl)
      (prodT (fromSingleT x) (fromPairT (y1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2))) =
    permT id (by simp; rfl) (fromSingleTContrFromPairT x (y1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.contrT_fromSingleT_fromPairT
declarations.statement:
lemma contrT_fromSingleT_fromPairT {c c2 : C}
    (x : V c)
    (y : V (S.τ c) ⊗[k] V c2) :
    contrT 1 0 1 (by simp; rfl)
      (prodT (fromSingleT x) (fromPairT y)) =
    permT id (by simp; rfl) (fromSingleTContrFromPairT x y)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairTContr
declarations.doc: The contraction of tensors with two indices defined categorically.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fromPairTContr {c c1 c2 : C}(x : V c1 ⊗[k] V c) (y : V (S.τ c) ⊗[k] V c2) :
    S.Tensor ![c1, c2]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairTContr_tmul_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairTContr_tmul_tmul {c c1 c2 : C} (x1 : V c1) (x2 : V c) (y1 : V (S.τ c))
    (y2 : V c2) : fromPairTContr (x1 ⊗ₜ[k] x2) (y1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2) =
    (S.contr c) (x2 ⊗ₜ[k] y1) • fromPairT (x1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_contr_fromPairT_eq_fromPairTContr_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_contr_fromPairT_eq_fromPairTContr_tmul (c c1 c2 : C)
    (x1 : V c1) (x2 : V c) (y1 : V (S.τ c))
    (y2 : V c2) :
    contrT 2 1 2 (by simp; rfl) (prodT (fromPairT (x1 ⊗ₜ[k] x2)) (fromPairT (y1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2))) =
    permT id (by simp; exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
    (fromPairTContr (x1 ⊗ₜ[k] x2) (y1 ⊗ₜ[k] y2))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_contr_fromPairT_eq_fromPairTContr
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_contr_fromPairT_eq_fromPairTContr (c c1 c2 : C)
    (x : V c1 ⊗[k] V c)
    (y : V (S.τ c) ⊗[k] V c2) :
    contrT 2 1 2 (by simp; rfl)
      (prodT (fromPairT x) (fromPairT y)) =
    permT id (by simp; exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩) (fromPairTContr x y)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_basis_repr
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_basis_repr {c c1 : C}
    (x : V c ⊗[k] V c1)
    (φ : ComponentIdx ![c, c1]) :
    (basis ![c, c1]).repr (fromPairT (S := S) x) φ =
    (Basis.tensorProduct (b c) (b c1)).repr x (φ 0, φ 1)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_apply_basis_repr
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_apply_basis_repr {c c1 : C}
    (b0 : basisIdx c) (b1 : basisIdx c1) :
    fromPairT (S := S) (b c b0 ⊗ₜ[k] b c1 b1) =
    Tensor.basis ![c, c1] (fun | 0 => b0 | 1 => b1)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromConstPair
declarations.doc: A constant two tensor (e.g. metric and unit).

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.actionT_fromConstPair
declarations.doc: Tensors formed by `fromConstPair` are invariant under the group action.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromMatrixT
declarations.doc:
Rank-two tensors and their component matrices, as a linear equivalence: `fromMatrixT c0 c1 M`
is the tensor with component matrix `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fromMatrixT (c0 c1 : C) :
    Matrix (basisIdx c0) (basisIdx c1) k ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor ![c0, c1]
